title: RFK Jr says Fauci prioritized 'getting on TV' over public health after revealing diary release
excerpt: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. unpacks Dr. Anthony Fauci's private diaries, exposing alleged lies about vaccine efficacy, masks, and natural immunity. Kennedy states Fauci's 'giddy narcissism' dr...
body_text:
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. unpacks Dr. Anthony Fauci's private diaries, exposing alleged lies about vaccine efficacy, masks, and natural immunity. Kennedy states Fauci's 'giddy narcissism' drove his self-promotion, leading to the 'mismanagement of this pandemic.'

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. condemned Dr. Anthony Fauci on Monday after revealing personal diary entries revealed the doctor’s fixation on fame during the COVID-19 pandemic.

"[Fauci’s] focus was on promoting himself, on getting on TV and not doing public health," Kennedy said on "The Ingraham Angle."

The journals, released by Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., chronicle Fauci's day-to-day life during the COVID-19 pandemic, detailing Fauci’s obsession with his newfound fame and his belief that it was "not hyperbole" to say he was "the most famous and talked about person in the country."

Kennedy, who said he is traumatized by Fauci’s falsehoods, said the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases did "incalculable" damage to public health and dismantled the public’s trust.

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

Kennedy said Fauci is to blame for Americans’ lack of trust in public health and added that "they shouldn’t" because they were "lied to." (Left (Alex Wong/Getty Images), Right (Kent Nishimura/Getty Images))

"[Fauci] was the expert that they elevated. And anybody who did not give complete blind faith to these expert opinions – which we now know were lies – was marginalized, vilified, demonized, censored," the HHS secretary told host Laura Ingraham.

Fauci, 85, became largely revered as "America’s doctor" as the public looked to him for guidance during 2020 COVID-19 shutdowns.

ANTHONY FAUCI'S PRIVATE DIARY AND EMAILS SHOW HE KNEW LOCKDOWNS FAILED AND PUSHED MASKS WITHOUT EVIDENCE

RFK Jr. strongly criticized the doctor’s "mismanagement" of the pandemic, emphasizing his role in placing the United States at the highest mortality rate in the world at 3,000 deaths per one million people.

Anthony Fauci, director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, listens during a Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee hearing in Washington, D.C., on Thursday, Nov. 4, 2021. Younger children across the U.S. became eligible to receive Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine after the head of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention granted final clearance for shots to begin. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Because of Dr. Fauci's leadership and other reasons, we had the highest mortality rate from COVID of any country in the world," he told Fox News. "We literally did worse than any nation in the world."

The HHS secretary recalled being de-platformed over questioning Fauci’s assertions about the origins of COVID-19, lamenting how many were "vilified" over spreading "misinformation" that was later deemed to be true.

SLACK MESSAGES RELEASED BY RAND PAUL APPEAR TO SHOW AUTHORS OF KEY COVID-19 ORIGIN PAPER HELD PRIVATE DOUBTS

"I pointed out that [COVID-19] almost certainly came from the Wuhan lab and… my Instagram was canceled with a million followers for misinformation," Kennedy explained. "I never put any misinformation up. I put up all the things that we now know are true and it was called misinformation."

Security personnel stand guard outside the Wuhan Institute of Virology in Wuhan as members of the World Health Organization (WHO) team investigating the origins of the COVID-19 coronavirus make a visit to the institute in Wuhan in China's central Hubei province on February 3, 2021. (Photo by Hector RETAMAL / AFP) (Photo by HECTOR RETAMAL/AFP via Getty Images) (Hector Retamal/AFP via Getty Images)

Kennedy pointed fingers at Fauci, saying he is to blame for Americans’ lack of trust in public health and added that "they shouldn’t" because they were "lied to."

He also took aim at legacy media organizations for what he described as suppressing dissenting views and vehemently defending Fauci.

"The press was part of this collaboration," RFK Jr said. "It was corrupt, and it did tremendous damage to the media in this country and to Americans’ faith in that very important democratic institution. It also did incalculable damage to public health."

Kennedy argued Fauci could potentially face perjury prosecution as the doctor faces congressional testimony Wednesday about his diary entries and handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

"There are many things that [Fauci] said that we know are lies, and Rand Paul presumably is going to ask him about those things, and if he lies again, then he could be subject to perjury prosecution," he said.

Nora Moriarty is a Writer at Fox News Digital.

title: J&J offers $5.5bn settlement in lawsuits claiming talc link to cancer
excerpt:
Johnson & Johnson (J&J) has agreed to pay $5.5bn to settle tens of thousands of lawsuits in the United States that allege its discontinued talc-based baby powder caused ovarian cancer.

The pharmaceut...
body_text:
Johnson & Johnson (J&J) has agreed to pay $5.5bn to settle tens of thousands of lawsuits in the United States that allege its discontinued talc-based baby powder caused ovarian cancer.

The pharmaceutical giant made the announcement on Monday, saying it covers about 69,000 cases in US federal and state courts, accounting for 99.75 percent of outstanding talc-related cases in the country.

The settlement will only be final once it is accepted by 95 percent of the claimants in state or federal courts.

Talc is a soft mineral and was once a staple ingredient in cosmetics and baby products, but its use has declined as concerns rose over its links to cancer.

In 2024, the World Health Organization classified talc as “probably carcinogenic to humans”.

J&J maintains that there is no evidence that talc causes cancer, but it stopped selling talc-based baby powder in the US in 2020 and worldwide in 2023.

In 2016, a US jury ordered J&J to pay $72m to the family of a woman who died of ovarian cancer, the first such case related to the use of the mineral in the country.

Though the case was overturned a year later, claims against the company have multiplied since, with juries across the US awarding the plaintiffs.

Erik Haas, J&J’s litigation head, said the agreement lets J&J “put this matter behind it”.

Lawyers representing the plaintiffs welcomed the settlement as a good resolution to a decade-long court battle.

The deal does not cover the United Kingdom, where the largest product liability case in UK history – covering more than 7,000 potential claimants – is being adjudicated.

Filed in October 2025, the UK case alleges that J&J knew that its talc could cause cancers, chiefly ovarian and mesothelioma, but continued to sell the product, a claim the company also denies.

The case has since gone before the UK High Court.

title: Kelsey Grammer admits it's 'exhausting' when movies try to alter history to fit modern tastes
excerpt: "Frasier" star Kelsey Grammer spoke on "The Katie Miller Podcast" about how Hollywood should respect historical and cultural accuracy, but also will likely be course correcting soon after so many flop...
body_text:
"Frasier" star Kelsey Grammer spoke on "The Katie Miller Podcast" about how Hollywood should respect historical and cultural accuracy, but also will likely be course correcting soon after so many flops.

FIRST ON FOX: "Frasier" star Kelsey Grammer spoke on "The Katie Miller Podcast" about how modern Hollywood keeps getting in its own way.

Podcaster Katie Miller, the wife of White House deputy chief of staff for policy Stephen Miller, observed, "Hollywood seems determined to reinvent nearly every classic, like ‘The Odyssey,’ and distort it just a little bit to fit their views. Have you watched ‘The Odyssey’?"

"I haven't seen ‘The Odyssey,’ so I'm not really too aware of that," Grammer admitted, but added that there are times when certain entertainment "hits me over the head" to the point where, "it's a little exhausting."

He noted that the past was less multicultural than Hollywood would like to portray it, saying, "I think old England is probably full of White people" and that "I think historical significance should be respected a little bit, culturally."

CHRISTOPHER NOLAN CONFIRMS BIZARRE 'THE ODYSSEY' CASTING CHOICES INCLUDING RAPPER TRAVIS SCOTT

Kelsey Grammer speaks onstage during a screening of "Frasier" Season 2 at Quad Cinema on Sept. 16, 2024, in New York City. (Roy Rochlin/Getty Images for Paramount+)

"Do you think Hollywood will ever get back there?" Miller asked.

"Yeah. Hollywood isn't very good at telling people what they have to see, you know, because then they flop,’ Grammer replied.

"But they've had, like, successive years of just flops," Miller replied.

One prominent example of a controversial adaptation that flopped was "Snow White," which reportedly netted Disney an approximately $170 million loss. Pixar — under parent company Disney — has tried to pivot away from a series of flops by cutting LGBTQ themes and warning not to make films inspired by the creators' own life stories.

Pixar Chief Creative Officer Pete Docter told The Wall Street Journal that he chose this pivot because "We’re making a movie, not hundreds of millions of dollars of therapy."

"Yeah. They're probably figuring it out. I think eventually flopping doesn't work so well," Grammer said. "We're not shooting a lot of movies these days. But I mean, I'm glad they made ‘The Odyssey.’ I mean, I don't know if they've, you know, pitched it too far in to our particular culture to divorce you from the idea of what actually happened."

FROM ‘SCREAM’ TO STREAM: JAMIE KENNEDY REVEALS HOW HOLLYWOOD LOST ITS WAY AND WHY HE WON'T GIVE UP ON LA

(L-R) Stephen Miller and Katie Miller attend the 2026 White House Correspondents' Dinner at Washington Hilton on April 25, 2026, in Washington, DC. (Paul Morigi/Getty Images)

In recent years, there have been numerous movies in the culture-war spotlight, ranging from remakes like "The Little Mermaid" and "Snow White" to adaptations of ancient history like "Cleopatra" and "The Odyssey."

Emily Wilson, who famously wrote what some call a feminist translation of Homer’s "The Odyssey" that helped influence the film, panned director Christopher Nolan’s adaptation for missing the spirit of the original heroic epic. The film has also been criticized for using modernized Americanized dialogue, reshaping the character of Odysseus as a more traumatized rather than heroic figure, and for removing many of the mythological aspects.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

General views of the TCL Chinese Theatre during opening weekend for Christopher Nolan's film "The Odyssey" in IMAX on July 18, 2026, in Hollywood, Calif. (GC Images)

In contrast to other controversial adaptations of beloved works, Nolan’s adaptation of "The Odyssey" has managed to become a box office hit, though audiences and critics remain divided over whether its bold creative choices improved the story or missed the mark.

Grammer's full interview with Miller will be published Tuesday night on the show's YouTube page.

Alexander Hall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Alexander.hall@fox.com.

title: NY Times reporter admits Trump's 'delusional' foes have wrongly written his political obituary many times
excerpt:

New York Times reporter ...
body_text:
New York Times reporter Jonathan Swan noted that President Donald Trump has proved his critics wrong time and time again after they predicted the end of his political career.

New York Times reporter Jonathan Swan suggested during a "60 Minutes Australia" interview released last week that President Donald Trump has "Napoleonic" ambition and a political survivability that should humble journalists.

Swan and fellow Times reporter Maggie Haberman discussed their new book, "Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump," and Swan offered speculation on the rest of the president's term and cautioned other journalists to have some humility.

"So there's still a sense that, even if Democrats take the House from Trump, they really can't touch him," Swan said in the interview. "And, like you said, his family's made a lot of money. He's wealthier than he's ever been. He has immunity conferred by the Supreme Court. And there's no prospect, even if he does get impeached, there's no prospect of a conviction."

"I think Donald Trump's obituary has been written so many times — his political obituary — by so many people," Swan continued. "And by this point, if you don't have some humility around that, I think, you know, you're operating in a fairly delusional way. This is someone who has incredible survival capacities, who's able to regenerate himself, and he's still got two and a half years left as the most powerful man on the planet, with no intention of receding at all."

HOW TRUMP SURVIVES: BATTLING THE MEDIA, FORMER ALLIES AND ASSASSINATION ATTEMPTS

For over a decade, even when he was not in office, President Donald Trump has dominated American politics, having led a movement that shook the political landscape. (Kent Nishimura/Reuters)

As he spoke about the future of Trump’s term, he noted that the president's next step may be taking on the Cuban regime.

"So there are many things he could do," he said. "The most obvious in foreign policy is Cuba. They've been looking at potential regime change in Cuba, but who knows? It's a big world out there, and we don't want to start being pundits and prognosticating."

Swan also described a past encounter at the White House that he suggested speaks volumes about Trump’s personal mindset and policies. As Trump met with Swan and Haberman, he had purportedly shown them a document he claimed was written by a historian.

"So it opens by saying Donald Trump is the most powerful man who's ever existed, ever lived on the planet, by far," Swan said. "And then it goes on to compare him to what Donald Trump said was, to us, the top ten. And it was Stalin, Mao, Hitler, Napoleon, Attila the Hun, Genghis Khan, the Caesars, Alexander the Great, Tamerlane ... there's probably one I'm missing."

TRUMP AIMS TO RESET WAR POWERS CLOCK WITH CONTROVERSIAL BID TO BYPASS CONGRESS

New York Times reporter Jonathan Swan claimed that President Trump showed him a document comparing himself to strongmen of the past, including Napoleon Bonaparte.  (VCG Wilson/Corbis via Getty Images)

"And it had nothing to do with morality," Swan continued. "The document didn't mention morality. It was about power and raw power."

The premise of the document, Swan said, was that Trump is the most powerful leader in history and is willing to use power in a way no previous president has done within their lifetime, which he noted was remarkably similar to the book he wrote about the administration.

Swan added further, "I think it's also that he wants to be a sort of Napoleonic ... you know, the person who only needs to be known by one name, who is the defining figure of our age. And so, when Trump thinks about himself in history, I don't think he's comparing himself to Bill Clinton or, you know, name your U.S. president — Eisenhower. I think it is to figures like Napoleon and that he wants to be the defining global figure of our age."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The White House responded to the interview by touting, "President Trump is fighting every day to deliver the strong, safe, and prosperous country that we all deserve. The only legacy President Trump is concerned with is making America greater than ever before." (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

In response to Swan's comments, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told Fox News Digital that "President Trump is fighting every day to deliver the strong, safe, and prosperous country that we all deserve. The only legacy President Trump is concerned with is making America greater than ever before."

Alexander Hall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Alexander.hall@fox.com.

title: Michigan progressive Abdul El-Sayed says ‘ogre’ remark not directed at rival
excerpt:
El-Sayed says in TV debate ‘ogre on a pike’ Zoom comment was in reference to John Fetterman, not Haley Stevens

The Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said his comments that progressi...
body_text:
El-Sayed says in TV debate ‘ogre on a pike’ Zoom comment was in reference to John Fetterman, not Haley Stevens

The Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said his comments that progressives need to put the head of an “ogre” on a pike was in reference to the US senator John Fetterman – not his opponent, Haley Stevens.

In a televised debate on Monday, the final head-to-head before the state’s 4 August primary, the moderator asked El-Sayed whether he regretted his comments made in a Zoom meeting, in which he said, according to leaked audio published by Politico: “Ideally you put one ogre on a pike, and then everyone else gets the message, and all of a sudden [it] starts to sound a lot different.”

The comments drew immediate backlash from several high-profile Democrats.

“Many people took offense to that,” the debate moderator Roop Raj noted. “Do you regret any of the comments that you’ve made?”

El-Sayed did not reply directly, but argued that he had stood up for civility, noting that he chided supporters who mocked Stevens’ accent.

“Look, I took to Twitter last week and said that the tone in which people talk about my opponent is unkind, and I asked anybody who supported me to not talk about her that way,” he said.

Speaking of “ogre” comments directly, El-Sayed said he was referencing Fetterman, a Pennsylvania Democrat who was elected as a progressive but has moved to the right since taking office. He and El-Sayed have clashed mightily over the senator’s increasingly robust support for Israel, and in recent weeks Fetterman has suggested he would leave the Democratic party if it became “anti-Israel” .

El-Sayed said in the debate: “I was referring to a guy named John Fetterman, who’s a senator from Pennsylvania who has done terrible things, got elected on a set of values, and is now completely throwing those values in the mud.”

Stevens quipped: “Thank you for clarifying that you didn’t call me an ogre.”

The Democratic primary to replace retiring senator Gary Peters has evolved into a proxy fight over the party’s future, pitting the establishment-backed moderate Stevens against El-Sayed, a progressive former Detroit health director.

The candidates have split sharply on the issue of Israel, with Stevens identifying as a “proud pro-Israel Democrat” and accepting substantial support from American Israel Public Affairs Committee. By contrast, El-Sayed has called Israel’s campaign in Gaza a “genocide” and has denounced US arms support for Israel.

Last week, Stevens picked up the endorsement of Michigan governor Gretchen Whitmer, who El-Sayed challenged unsuccessfully in the 2018 gubernatorial primary. El-Sayed has rallied the party’s left flank, and has been endorsed by the independent senator Bernie Sanders and New York congressmember Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

The dueling coalitions have turned Michigan’s closely watched Senate contest into a clear test of whether the twin forces of anti-Washington sentiment and progressive energy can overcome broad institutional support in a presidential battleground state.

Asked about whether he would call himself a progressive or a democratic socialist, El-Sayed replied: “I’m not a socialist. I’m just a capitalist who understands how capitalism works. The biggest threat to capitalism was never the idea of government regulation. It was always monopoly.”

The contest – one of the few open-seat races this cycle – is widely viewed as central to the battle for Senate control. Donald Trump won Michigan in 2024, making it among Republicans’ most promising pick-up opportunities. Former congressman Mike Rogers, who narrowly lost Michigan’s 2024 Senate race to Elissa Slotkin, cleared the Republican field early and has spent months preparing for the general election while Democrats have waged an expensive and increasingly bitter primary.

Earlier on Monday, Rogers appeared on stage with Trump at a rally in Milford, Michigan, where he promised to help the president enact his agenda, if elected.

title: Houthis want to copy Iran’s Hormuz control in the Red Sea: Yemeni FM
excerpt:
Houthis claim Saudi drone downed over northwestern Yemen

Yemen’s Houthi movement is aiming to replicate Iran’s ⁠strategy in the Strait of Hormuz by controlling shipping flows in the Red Sea’s Bab al-...
body_text:
Houthis claim Saudi drone downed over northwestern Yemen

Yemen’s Houthi movement is aiming to replicate Iran’s ⁠strategy in the Strait of Hormuz by controlling shipping flows in the Red Sea’s Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the Yemeni government’s top diplomat warns.

“The Houthis want to copy the Iranian model , and this will shut down two main straits, the gateways into the ⁠Gulf and Red Sea,” the foreign minister-designate for the internationally recognised Yemeni government, Afrah al-Zouba, told journalists on Monday.

Speaking at the Yemeni embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, al-Zouba said the Iran-backed Houthis have been emboldened due to the insufficient international response to their activities in the region.

Bab al-Mandeb Strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the wider Indian Ocean, and – much like the Strait of Hormuz – a significant portion of the global economy depends on the unimpeded flow of maritime traffic through it.

Approximately 30 percent of global container traffic passes through the Red Sea, and 12 to 15 percent of overall global trade.

Yemen’s geography gives whoever controls the country’s west a commanding influence over traffic through Bab al-Mandeb.

Data suggests that shipping through the Red Sea is already declining, with just 11 commodity vessels passing through it on Sunday.

Al-Zouba’s comments come as tensions between the Houthis on one side and Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s internationally recognised government on the other escalate.

Earlier in July, the Houthis declared a maritime siege on Red Sea shipping to and from Saudi Arabia, and launched missiles and drones at the kingdom.

Riyadh has since launched air strikes on Yemen’s key port city of Hodeidah, held by the Houthis.

July’s escalation is the biggest since a truce was agreed to in 2022 and came amid a resurgence of US attacks on Iran.

Al-Zouba said Yemen’s government, which Saudi Arabia backs, is prepared for an escalation, and that fire was being exchanged along the front line where Houthi-controlled territory meets government-controlled areas, but that no offensive had been launched.

Nearly 20 fighters from both sides died earlier this month during clashes between the Houthis and government forces around Hodeidah.

Hundreds of thousands of people have died in Yemen since war broke out in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, and then-President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi eventually fled to Riyadh.

Saudi Arabia led an Arab coalition in a campaign to dislodge the Houthis from 2015 up to the 2022 truce.

As of 2026, the Houthis remain in power in the capital and other parts of Yemen. Meanwhile, tensions between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, which Riyadh accuses of backing a southern separatist group in Yemen, have affected developments on the ground.

Yemeni civilians have paid the heaviest price, with an estimated 377,000 dying between 2015 and the beginning of 2022, most of them from war’s knock-on impacts, such as famine and disease.

title: Australia news live: Jacinta Allan leadership challenge: Victorian premier due to hold press conference as rival Ben Carroll focuses on ‘talking to colleagues’
excerpt:
Allan says she believes she would have won leadership spill. Follow updates live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Jacinta Allan, the Victorian premier, will step down amid...
body_text:
Allan says she believes she would have won leadership spill. Follow updates live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Jacinta Allan, the Victorian premier, will step down amid a leadership spill.

double quotation markAfter speaking with my colleagues overnight, I’ve made the difficult decision to step aside.

Should Ben Carroll emerge as our next Labor leader and Labor premier, he will have my congratulations and unqualified support.

I am making this because it’s the right thing by the Labor party, and by the Victorian people.

Allan says she is “immensely proud” of her time in office, which has lasted 1,036 days:

double quotation markLet’s be honest – this gig has been tough. … I leave immensely proud of what we have achieved these past three years.

I inherited a rising crime rate. My team and I toughened bail laws. … Crime is now falling for the first time since Covid. I inherited a budget deficit. …

Making life easier and more affordable became my mission.

Jacinta Allan, the Victorian premier, will step down amid a leadership spill.

double quotation markAfter speaking with my colleagues overnight, I’ve made the difficult decision to step aside.

Should Ben Carroll emerge as our next Labor leader and Labor premier, he will have my congratulations and unqualified support.

I am making this because it’s the right thing by the Labor party, and by the Victorian people.

Key Jacinta Allan supporter says premier will not contest leadership spill

We’ve just heard from a key Allan supporter who says the premier Jacinta Allan will not contest the leadership spill bought against her by deputy Ben Carroll.

Jacinta Allan is expected to speak at a press conference in just a few moments, at 9.30am Melbourne time.

Colin Brooks arrives at Victorian parliament

Colin Brooks – one of the six ministers who told the premier yesterday she no longer had their support – has just arrived at parliament. Asked if he’d be supporting Ben Carroll in the spill, he said:

double quotation markI’ll be voting for integrity in the Labor party and a royal commission.

Queensland won’t adopt new AusAlert system until next year at the earliest

Queensland won’t adopt the federal government’s new AusAlert system until months after the planned nationwide rollout of the system in October.

The state’s minister for fire and disaster recovery, Ann Leahy, told ABC local radio this morning the “earliest” the state could adopt the new system would be April next year.

The state says the new system won’t work in some regional areas, because it doesn’t use fixed landline phone lines.

“In October we will be right in the middle of our fire season, so we will be continuing with the existing system,” Leahy said.

double quotation markThe earliest we could go across to the AusAlert would be in April next year, because we simply know we have people trained to use the existing system.

Greens senator says it was a ‘good day’ after court upholds finding Pauline Hanson engaged in racial discrimination

Greens senator Mehreen Faruqi said it was a “good day” yesterday after a court decision to uphold the finding that One Nation leader Pauline Hanson engaged in racial discrimination when she tweeted that she should “pack your bags and piss off back to Pakistan”.

Faruqi spoke to RN Breakfast this morning, saying:

double quotation markIt was a good day yesterday for people of colour, for Muslims, and for migrants in this country. And, you know, this is a win. And I have always said that this case was taken to court on behalf of everyone who has been told to go back to where you came from …

It is a strong form of racism. It is a statement that undermines people’s sense of belonging and treats them as a second-class citizen. And it has a massive impact.

Faruqi said she would be “prepared” if the case is taken to the high court, saying Hanson was “welcome to do that”.

The energy minister, Lily D’Ambrosio, is another key backer of Jacinta Allan and says that hasn’t changed:

double quotation markShe has my full support … We have a caucus meeting as we always do, and the premier is committed to her job. And as far as I’m concerned, she’ll continue in that role.

‘Personal loyalty’ always important, former Victoria health minister says

Former Victorian health minister Mary-Anne Thomas, who earlier this year announced she would resign at the November election, says she will not support a spill this morning:

double quotation markPersonal loyalty has always been very important to me, and if there is a spill motion this morning, I will not be supporting it.

double quotation markJacinta Allan has served this state with real leadership. She’s always had the people of Victoria at the heart of everything that she does, I’ve known Jacinta for a very long time, and I have a great deal of admiration for her.

The deputy premier, Ben Carroll, who is challenging Jacinta Allan for the Victorian Labor leadership in a few hours time, has arrived at parliament and made a brief statement to reporters:

double quotation markI will have more to say later. Right now, my focus is on talking to my colleagues.

Some early remarks before the Victorian leadership spill

Minister Steve Dimopoulos – a key supporter of Allan – refused to comment on the spill as he arrived:

double quotation markI’m going to respect all of the process and respect the processes means not commenting before the process.

Asked about the mood within the caucus, he said: “I think the party has been good and sorting things out this is what today will be.”

double quotation markThe premier’s always had my support but there’s a process today that will work that out.

Labor MPs have begun arriving at Victorian parliament this morning for a caucus meeting where the premier, Jacinta Allan, will be challenged by her deputy, Ben Carroll.

Among them are the environment minister, Enver Erdogan, who has told reporters on their way in that there is a “case for change”.

Pressed on what needs to change, he says:

double quotation markI think we know some of these issues have been aired publicly, but I think we need stronger action on crime and corruption in the state.

Asked whether there needed to be a royal commission into allegations of corruption on Big Build construction sites, he replied: “Yes.”

The search for a missing baby has resumed after the bodies of a mother and her toddler were pulled from the ocean below rugged cliffs off South Australia’s Limestone Coast,

Police are scouring waters off Port MacDonnell in a desperate search for the child after receiving a call to an abandoned car left with its engine running near Cape Northumberland about 11.15am on Monday.

Officers spotted the bodies of a woman and small child in the ocean a short time later.

They have been identified as a 36-year-old woman from Compton, near Mount Gambier, and her toddler.

Officers from the Water Operations Unit, CFS and SES volunteers will help with the search. Predicted bad weather could hamper search efforts on the water on Tuesday, but police said they would still conduct searches of the coastline on foot and using thermal imaging drones.

title: 'Baywatch' star Brooks Nader suffers wardrobe malfunction during Saint-Tropez getaway
excerpt: Brooks Nader tells Fox News Digital about growing up with conservative parents who banned two-piece bikinis and reveals why her "Baywatch" swimsuit gets the family seal of approval at FOX Upfront 2026...
body_text:
Brooks Nader tells Fox News Digital about growing up with conservative parents who banned two-piece bikinis and reveals why her "Baywatch" swimsuit gets the family seal of approval at FOX Upfront 2026 red carpet.

Brooks Nader has seemingly been everywhere this summer.

Between filming Fox's upcoming "Baywatch" reboot in Los Angeles and hopping from one European hotspot to another, the 29-year-old model has kept fans updated every step of the way.

This week, Nader added another memorable moment to the itinerary.

BROOKS NADER NARROWLY AVOIDS WARDROBE MALFUNCTION MINUTES BEFORE 'BAYWATCH' REBOOT RED CARPET

Brooks Nader suffered an accidental wardrobe malfunction after enjoying a beach day at the iconic Club 55 in Saint-Tropez. (Aissaoui Nacer/Splash by Shutterstock)

After spending the afternoon dining at the iconic Club 55 in Saint-Tropez and cooling off with a swim, Nader experienced an unexpected fashion mishap. As she made her way back across the sand, her leopard-print halter playsuit briefly slipped, exposing her chest before she quickly adjusted the look.

Despite the fashion mishap, Nader appeared unfazed as she continued enjoying the glamorous beach day.

Nader gave followers a behind-the-scenes look aboard a luxury yacht through a series of Instagram Stories, including one that showed her posing in the same leopard-print halterneck playsuit after sunset.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Kneeling across cream-colored lounge cushions, Nader flipped her blonde hair over one shoulder while overlooking the Mediterranean. Another shot captured her sitting on the yacht with the sparkling coastline behind her, showing off the plunging animal-print look accented with a colorful jeweled brooch at the waist.

Brooks Nader shared a behind-the-scenes look at her Saint-Tropez getaway aboard a luxury yacht. (Brooks Nader/Instagram)

A change of scenery also meant a change of outfit.

In another Instagram Story, Nader traded the leopard-print ensemble for a casual white two-piece while walking barefoot up an elegant wooden staircase. She paired a fitted white tank top with cheeky white shorts that read "Saint-Tropez French Riviera" across the back.

BROOKS NADER WOWS IN ICONIC RED ONE-PIECE BATHING SUIT AS 'BAYWATCH' REBOOT FILMS BEACH SCENES

Before leaving France, the model admitted she wasn't ready for the trip to end.

Sharing another Story as she departed the yacht, Nader filmed her friends waving goodbye before writing, "Torture leaving my fave place & peeps, back to work I go."

She also documented the vacation on TikTok, including a playful video filmed aboard the yacht set to a trending Melania Trump sound.

Brooks Nader embraced casual style while vacationing in Saint-Tropez. (Brooks Nader/Instagram)

BROOKS NADER FLAUNTS HER TONED ABS IN BLACK BIKINI WHILE FILMING HER REALITY SHOW

As it turns out, wardrobe malfunctions have become somewhat of an unexpected trademark for the model.

Last year, Nader made headlines after unexpectedly bleeding through a white skirt while attending Wimbledon. Rather than hide the mishap, she leaned into the viral moment, sharing it on TikTok, where the video amassed nearly 200,000 likes before ultimately leading to a partnership with U by Kotex.

Her latest European getaway comes during an especially busy stretch in both her personal and professional life.

According to People, Nader is currently single after previously being linked to actor Taron Egerton. A source told the outlet that while she's been enjoying dating, her attention is firmly on work.

"Brooks is totally single right now. She's been going out on dates and having fun, but her main focus is Baywatch," the source told People.

Brooks Nader has spent the summer balancing filming with getaways. (GC Images)

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The insider added that Nader is currently balancing production on Fox's upcoming "Baywatch" reboot alongside filming the second season of her Hulu and Freeform reality series, "Love Thy Nader."

Nader also recently dismissed romance rumors herself, telling TMZ she and Egerton "never were" dating and insisting she's "just single, having fun, always."

Before that, the model dated her former "Dancing with the Stars" partner Gleb Savchenko following the end of her marriage to advertising executive Billy Haire. She has also been linked to tennis stars Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner.

title: Pro Bowl player requests trade from Tampa Bay Buccaneers on eve of training camp amid contract dispute
excerpt:
New York Giants HC John Harbaugh said that

As negotiation tactics go, asking for a trade the day before training camp opens is the NFL equivalent of reaching for the nuclear codes before deciding to ...
body_text:
New York Giants HC John Harbaugh said that

As negotiation tactics go, asking for a trade the day before training camp opens is the NFL equivalent of reaching for the nuclear codes before deciding to type them in. But that's exactly what Tampa Bay Buccaneers nose tackle Vita Vea has done.

The two-time Pro Bowl player has grown so frustrated with contract discussions this offseason that he's decided he doesn't see a future with the team, and has asked to be traded, a league source confirmed to Fox News Digital.

That doesn't mean a trade will happen. Vea is under contract for the 2026 season and is scheduled to make up to $18 million if he can play all 17 games in the final year of his current contract.

Atlanta Falcons quarterback Kirk Cousins (18) scrambles away from Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea (50) during the first half of an NFL football game Thursday, Oct. 3, 2024, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Butch Dill)

A.J. BROWN HEADED TO NEW ENGLAND TO REUNITE WITH MIKE VRABEL AFTER A SEASON OF EAGLES UNHAPPINESS

The Bucs aren't simply going to hold a fire sale to avoid the trade talk distraction, per a source.

Vea wants more money and points to the fact he is currently the 19th-highest-paid interior defensive lineman in the league. And he believes he is much better than the 19th-best defensive lineman in the league.

Vea is, for all intents and purposes, the structural centerpiece of the Tampa Bay defense. He is arguably the team's best run defender and, as all NFL defensive coordinators often note, if a defense cannot stop the run it is unable to do much of anything else.

Vea provides a rare combination of size, power to movement to control the middle of the formation from his nose tackle spot. At 6-foot-4 and 347 pounds, Vea has anchored against double-teams for much of his recent years.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea sacks Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) during the first half of an NFL wild-card football game, Monday, Jan. 16, 2023, in Tampa, Fla. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)

Despite this attention, he is able to clog interior rushing lanes and prevent offensive linemen from climbing cleanly to the second level of Tampa Bay’s defense. Since becoming a full-time starter in 2019, he has helped the Buccaneers establish one of the NFL’s most consistently productive run defenses.

From 2019 through most of the 2024 season, Tampa Bay ranked first in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game at 94.1, first in yards allowed per carry at 4.0 and finished in the top five against the run in five of six seasons, including No. 1 finishes in 2019 and 2020.

COWBOYS LOCK IN GEORGE PICKENS WITH $27.3M FRANCHISE TAG DESPITE FAILING TO REACH LONG-TERM CONTRACT

Vea played only five games in 2020 due to a fractured ankle, but he's proven durable ever since. He has started 78 games in the past five seasons.

Vea’s individual production shows he is more than a traditional space-eating nose tackle but he set a career high with seven sacks in 2024, then added 4.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss and 13 quarterback hits in 2025.

His 2024 pass-rush production made Tampa Bay one of only three teams that season with two defensive tackles recording at least seven sacks, as Vea and Calijah Kancey both reached that mark.

TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Vita Vea #50 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrates after beating the Chicago Bears 38-3 in the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 24, 2021 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images)

Vea was selected to the Pro Bowl following the 2021 and 2024 seasons, earned a place on the NFL Players Association’s Top 100 list entering 2025 and was a key member of Tampa Bay’s Super Bowl LV championship team.

This trade request creates issues for the Bucs.

It's possible Vea, who reported but did not take part in the teams mandatory minicamp and missed the rest of the offseason program, might decide to simply hold in to start training camp – that is to say, he shows up but doesn't practice.

The Buccaneers are already managing the high-stakes contract negotiations with quarterback Baker Mayfield as their top contract issue. So dealing with a very large star defender who has publicly let it be known he wants out is not great for the team.

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

title: PM praises Sally McManus and Michele O’Neil as ‘giants’ as they resign from ACTU
excerpt:
Secretary and president of Australian Council of Trade Unions announced  surprise departures on Monday evening

The leadership of the trade union movement is set for a major shakeup after the secretar...
body_text:
Secretary and president of Australian Council of Trade Unions announced  surprise departures on Monday evening

The leadership of the trade union movement is set for a major shakeup after the secretary and president of the Australian Council of Trade Unions announced their surprise departures.

The ACTU’s secretary, Sally McManus, and its president, Michele O’Neil, revealed on Monday night they would be stepping down after eight years together. Anthony Albanese described both as personal friends and “giants of the labour movement”.

The first all-female leadership team in the ACTU’s 99-year history, the influential pair played a major role in shaping the Albanese government’s workplace agenda.

They successfully campaigned for the right to disconnect law, same job, same pay protections, wage theft criminalisation and ensuring minimum pay, insurance and safety standards for gig economy workers.

The ACTU recently began targeting Pauline Hanson, in a clear sign the union movement now considers One Nation – rather than the Coalition – the biggest political threat to Labor and economic risk for working people.

McManus will depart in August while O’Neil will help the new secretary settle in before leaving before the end of the year.

In a farewell video posted to social media on Monday night, the pair said it was time for renewal.

“Union membership is growing and workers have over 47 new workplace rights,” McManus said. “But, of course, there are still big challenges with cost-of-living pressures, AI and billionaires who have too much wealth and power.”

In a statement, the prime minister said McManus and O’Neil’s “tireless advocacy and strong leadership” had put working families “in a stronger financial position today than they would otherwise be”.

“It is fitting that Sally and Michele announce they’re stepping down from their respective positions at a time when there have been significant wage increases in critical and long-undervalued sectors, the gender pay gap is at a record low and union membership is growing for the first time in decades,” Albanese said.

Speaking to ABC radio’s RN breakfast on Tuesday morning, O’Neil said it was the “right time” to leave, and that new leadership would be “the best thing for workers” and the “best thing for the union movement”.

title: US influencer ‘couldn’t seem to get away’ from husband accused of killing her, ex-partner says
excerpt:
Police believe Sara Gilson was killed by husband Jeremiah Duffy after she accused him on TikTok of child sexual abuse

Sara Gilson, the social media influencer who was killed after she publicly accuse...
body_text:
Police believe Sara Gilson was killed by husband Jeremiah Duffy after she accused him on TikTok of child sexual abuse

Sara Gilson, the social media influencer who was killed after she publicly accused her husband of child sexual abuse, “couldn’t seem to get away” from Jeremiah Duffy despite filing multiple protective orders, Gilson’s ex-husband said in an interview.

“She had been stuck in a relationship where domestic abuse seemed ‘OK’,”Lyle Landers told People. “I had begged her for five years to get away from him. I had offered to help her, in any way I could, to get away from him. But he seemed to have some sort of control over her, and she couldn’t seem to get away.”

Gilson publicly accused her husband, Jeremiah Duffy, of child sexual abuse in a video posted to TikTok on 11 July. Twelve days later, police received a call from a screaming Gilson, in which an apparent gunshot was heard. Police found the bodies of Gilson and Duffy at her home in Owasso, Oklahoma – both with gunshot wounds to the head.

Police suspect Duffy killed Gilson, then turned the gun on himself.

Landers, the father of Gilson’s two children, told People he had for years urged her to abandon Duffy.

“She was a wonderful mother and would die for her children. In fact, her trying to protect children is what ultimately led to her death,” Landers added.

Court records reported by the local press appear to support Landers’ concerns. Gilson filed for protective orders twice in 2021, according to the Oklahoman. Judges dismissed them after she did not appear in court.

This month, Gilson filed for another protective order, which was granted. The judge ordered Duffy out of Gilson’s home and required him to stay at least 100 yards away from her and her house. Gilson wrote in her application that Duffy had threatened suicide and possessed a firearm.

In a separate case, the mother of a 15-year-old girl asked a court to grant another protective order against Duffy. The woman said Duffy, a basketball coach, was seen kissing and touching her daughter after another coach walked in on them. Duffy had also sent the teen girl inappropriate text messages, asked her to join him in his hotel room on a trip, and paid her money to keep her from disclosing his behavior, the mother said.

“Similar conduct by this coach towards this particular juvenile player was reported to have occurred over an extended period of time, in multiple law enforcement jurisdictions, across multiple states prior to this incident,” police said, according to NBC News.

The teen’s parent went to a police station to report the allegations. Police attempted to apprehend Duffy at the school where the allegations took place, but he had left, according to Nick Boatman, a spokesperson for Owasso police.

Over the next 24 hours, police across multiple jurisdictions attempted to locate Duffy by pinging cellphone towers. The Muskogee sheriff’s department attempted to locate him by flying a drone near a tower that his phone had pinged.

“He stayed just enough ahead of us that we couldn’t track him down that night,” Boatman said.

But because the alleged crimes took place on Cherokee land and Duffy was a member of the Osage tribe, Owasso police referred investigation into alleged lewd behavior toward a minor to the US attorney’s office in Tulsa, which has jurisdiction over crimes on tribal land.

Neither the US attorney’s office nor the FBI field office in Tulsa immediately responded to requests for comment.

title: WNBA love feud explodes as NaLyssa Smith fires back at DiJonai Carrington's cheating claims
excerpt:
In a recent sit-down with ESPN, Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark is finally breaking her silence on the media's "false characterization" of her and the non-stop off-the-court drama in the WNBA.

...
body_text:
In a recent sit-down with ESPN, Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark is finally breaking her silence on the media's "false characterization" of her and the non-stop off-the-court drama in the WNBA.

Las Vegas Aces forward NaLyssa Smith went live on Twitch to respond after ex-girlfriend DiJonai Carrington accused her of a multi-player cheating scandal.

During a livestream, Smith refused to confirm or deny the allegations, instead questioning why the Chicago Sky guard chose to air their private history a year after their breakup.

Carrington launched the feud on Threads by alleging Smith cheated on her with Aces teammate Deja Kelly, Atlanta Dream guard Aaliyah Nye and others.

WNBA ROCKED BY MULTI-PLAYER CHEATING SCANDAL AS DIJONAI CARRINGTON CALLS OUT EX NALYSSA SMITH

Deja Kelly #2 of the Las Vegas Aces poses for a portrait during the team's media day at Vu Studios in Las Vegas, Nev., on May 8, 2025. (Getty Images)

Aaliyah Nye #13 of the Las Vegas Aces is filmed for an in-arena player intro video during the team's media day at Vu Studios in Las Vegas, Nev., on May 8, 2025. (Getty Images)

"Whether she cheated on me and I cheated on her, why are we bringing that to the internet a year later when nobody did anything to anybody? Whether she cheated on me or I cheated on her, that has nothing to do with anybody," Smith said. "Like what? That don't even make sense. And to bring it to the internet a year later, is crazy. Just for fun? That's ridiculous, especially when you're in a happy, healthy relationship."

Smith also criticized Carrington for dragging Kelly and Nye into the public dispute.

WNBPA SAYS IT DID NOT ASK WNBA TO DROP USA 250 ALL-STAR PATCH AFTER UNION OFFICER PUBLICLY OBJECTED

"Then, to bring up folks name that has nothing to do with anything. These folks is minding their business. These folks woke up to this s**t on a random Sunday night of these type of allegations," Smith said. "I think that's very weird."

Dallas Wings guard DiJonai Carrington gets held by forward NaLyssa Smith during a game against the Chicago Sky on May 31, 2025, at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Detailing the in-person confrontation that preceded Carrington's social media outburst, Smith claimed Carrington started an argument that ended with security stepping in.

"Here goes DiJonai. 'You talkin to that b*tch. You talkin to that b*tch.' B*tch this. B*tch that. I'm like 'Why I gotta be a b*tch?' Literally on my grandmother's grave, I'm like 'Damn why I gotta be a b*tch.' That's how the whole thing started," Smith said. "I'm literally like 'Who's a b*tch?' So, then it causes commotion and I'm just like 'Damn now what?' I look like the problem. So, then security come and he's like 'Alright y'all gonna have to leave.' Mind y'all, I'm the victim."

Smith also denied online claims that she showed up uninvited to keep tabs on Carrington.

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

"I didn't do 'none.' I'm sitting on the couch posting, minding my business. I didn't do nothing to nobody," Smith said. "So, the fact that people are trying to create this narrative of 'Lyss came somewhere uninvited and she came here just to spy on folks. Y'all gotta stop all that lying."

Baylor guard DiJonai Carrington (21) shoots between Oklahoma guard Skylar Vann (24) and guard Gabby Gregory (12) in the first half of an NCAA college basketball game Sunday, Feb. 21, 2021, in Norman, Okla. (AP Photo/Sue Ogrocki)

Smith suggested alcohol contributed to Carrington's outburst.

"I guess the liquor, the cameras, her crowd, I guess she got some type of, somebody boosted her up to gain some confidence," Smith said. "But at the end of the day, that was some bulls–t. We came to the spot. Folks was chilling. Nobody did nothing to nobody."

The former Baylor teammates will meet on the court Aug. 1, when Carrington's Sky host Smith and the Aces in Chicago.
