title: Newborn vanished after secret birth, parents allegedly claimed baby 'was a prank': cops
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Florida couple accused of claiming their missing infant never existed has been arrested in North Carolina after a ye...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Florida couple accused of claiming their missing infant never existed has been arrested in North Carolina after a yearlong investigation into the child’s presumed death.

Leon Alejandro Jr., 21, and Samantha Feliz, 20, both of Hollywood, Florida, were arrested Wednesday in Rockingham, North Carolina, where investigators say they fled while Hollywood police investigated the disappearance of their infant.

The pair were taken into custody by investigators with the Richmond County Sheriff's Office and the U.S. Marshals Service and booked into the Richmond County Jail on fugitive of justice warrants. They are being held without bond pending extradition to Florida.

Hollywood police began investigating the case in early 2025 after learning Feliz allegedly gave birth sometime between Dec. 6, 2024, and Jan. 5, 2025, according to the Richmond County Sheriff's Office.

DNA FROM SODA BOTTLE ALLEGEDLY LINKS MASSACHUSETTS WOMAN TO 1985 MURDER OF 'BABY BOY DOE'

Leon Alejandro Jr., 21, and Samantha Angeline Feliz, 20, were arrested in North Carolina and are awaiting extradition to Florida on multiple felony charges related to the disappearance of their infant. (Richmond County Sheriff's Office - N.C. via Facebook)

Authorities said the birth was concealed and happened somewhere other than a hospital.

Investigators said family members saw the couple with the baby during the child's first month of life. After that, authorities said, the infant was never seen again.

According to an arrest warrant obtained by WPLG, investigators believe the child, identified only by the initials A.F., was last photographed on Jan. 5, 2025. Detectives wrote that the infant appeared "visibly ill and malnourished" and showed "no signs of life" in what they described as the final known image.

The warrant also alleges investigators searched multiple locations with cadaver dogs but were unable to locate the child's remains, according to the outlet.

MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PARTNER ARRESTED IN MEXICO NEARLY TWO YEARS AFTER FLEEING WITH THEIR TWO CHILDREN

Investigators with the Richmond County Sheriff's Office and the U.S. Marshals Service arrested the Florida couple at a property near Rockingham, North Carolina. (Richmond County Sheriff's Office - N.C. Facebook)

Authorities allege Alejandro and Feliz repeatedly denied the child existed, telling relatives the baby "was a prank" and later claiming the pregnancy had been a "hoax" intended to scam family members out of money, WPLG reported, citing the arrest warrant.

According to the outlet, investigators said photographs showed Feliz visibly pregnant, while text messages discussed the pregnancy and the baby.

Detectives also reportedly recovered baby clothing, a positive pregnancy test and what appeared to be blood-stained towels from a storage unit tied to the couple. DNA testing later determined blood recovered from the baby clothing and towels belonged to a biological child of Alejandro and Feliz, according to the warrant.

Despite the lack of a birth certificate or medical records, investigators said they developed enough evidence to charge both suspects with aggravated manslaughter of a child, tampering with or fabricating physical evidence, failure to report a death to the medical examiner, providing false information concerning a missing child and making false reports to law enforcement.

Authorities allege the couple fled Florida and were living on property belonging to one of Alejandro's relatives in Richmond County when investigators located and arrested them July 22.

'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN

Hollywood, Florida, lies on the Florida beach between Fort Lauderdale and Miami, and was named after the showbiz town in California. (fotog via Getty Images)

Richmond County Sheriff Mark Gulledge praised the multi-agency effort that led to the arrests.

"This is a prime example of agencies nationwide collaborating to uphold justice," Gulledge said in a statement.

Authorities have not publicly released additional details about what investigators believe happened to the infant.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Richmond County Sheriff's Office for any additional updates on the investigation, but did not immediately receive a response.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Jalen Brunson's Knicks status on full display as he walks in venue with wife while Nets star checks guest list
excerpt: After a 53-year wait, the New York Knicks captured their first NBA championship, sparking celebrations across New York City. Thousands of fans lined the streets of Manhattan for a historic ticker-tape...
body_text:
After a 53-year wait, the New York Knicks captured their first NBA championship, sparking celebrations across New York City. Thousands of fans lined the streets of Manhattan for a historic ticker-tape parade, turning a Thursday workday into a spontaneous holiday as the city honored its victorious team.

There are levels to everything, even when you are a professional athlete.

Just look at what happened when Jalen Brunson, an NBA champion with the New York Knicks, and Michael Porter Jr., who stars for the Brooklyn Nets on the other side of town, arrived at a venue in a video that has since gone viral.

Brunson, who was alongside his wife, Ali, happened to arrive at a World Cup after-party hosted by Justin Bieber in New York City at the same time as Michael Porter Jr., who was with his former Denver Nuggets teammate Peyton Watson.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson and Brooklyn Nets star Michael Porter Jr. had two different experiences at a nightclub in New York City. (GETTY)

Porter may make more than Brunson per season ($40.8 million per season compared to $37.7 million), but the latter has achieved the ultra-rare "King of New York" status.

That means Brunson and his wife don’t need to wait in a queue or make sure they’re on a guest list when arriving anywhere. Porter, on the other hand, had to do just that.

TRUMP HYPES JALEN BRUNSON AFTER KNICKS SECURE NBA CHAMPIONSHIP: 'A SUPERSTAR WAS BORN'

The video shows Porter and Watson, who are both champions in their own right after winning the NBA title in 2023 with the Nuggets, needing to check in at the front door of the venue.

Meanwhile, the Brunson couple walked right through the front door, as camera flashes lit up the area right away.

Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks drives on Michael Porter Jr. of the Denver Nuggets during the first quarter at Ball Arena in Denver on Thursday, March 21, 2024. (Denver Post)

"Mr. Brunson, how are you?" the security guard at the front door said to the NBA Finals MVP.

In New York lore, playing for the Knicks carries a certain weight compared to being in Brooklyn with the Nets. For one, the Knicks are the more iconic franchise, playing in "The Mecca" that is Madison Square Garden. The history, the rabid fans, and of course, this particular group led by Brunson winning the first title in 53 years, has electrified the city more than the Nets have.

The Nets moved from New Jersey to Brooklyn in 2012, and though they’ve had some teams with solid NBA All-Stars since then, they are never expected to take over the percentage of Knicks fans across the five boroughs.

The Nets have been in rebuild mode for the past three seasons, including Porter Jr.’s first during the 2025-26 campaign with Brooklyn. While he enjoyed career highs in points (24.2 per game) and assists (3), the team went 20-62 to finish third-to-last in the Eastern Conference.

Jalen Brunson, his wife Ali Marks and their daughter, Jordyn James Brunson, are seen at the New York Knicks ticker-tape parade along the Canyon of Heroes on June 18, 2026, in New York City. (GC Images)

Porter Jr. and Watson didn’t have trouble getting in after checking with the guest list coordinator, but the comparison between the Knicks and Nets got its latest debate topic.

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Ebola infections in DR Congo surge to 3,200, with 1,405 deaths
excerpt:
The number of people infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has risen to 3,200, according to government data, including at least 1,405 deaths.

The data was released on Sunday as ...
body_text:
The number of people infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has risen to 3,200, according to government data, including at least 1,405 deaths.

The data was released on Sunday as medics struggle to contain the DRC’s 17th Ebola outbreak, with infections surging by about 1,000 in just 10 days.

The outbreak, declared on May 15, is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment.

The World Health Organization said nearly 90 percent of cases have been reported in the northeastern province of Ituri, which borders South Sudan and Uganda.

The United Nations agency says the virus is in five provinces, including two new provinces where it has spread recently.

“In many cases the humanitarian community wants to help, but the real challenge is getting there”, said Hedley Tah of the UN Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS), which flies medics and response teams to crisis front lines.

In addition to moving aid workers to stricken areas, Tah added that UNHAS is “moving samples for lab testing to ensure traceability can continue”.

Authorities said that improved detection and testing had helped identify more infections.

The outbreak could last several more months, and strikes by healthcare workers demanding unpaid wages have disrupted response efforts in some hospitals.

Ebola, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids and causes hemorrhagic fever, has killed more than 15,000 people across Africa over the past 50 years.

Scientists are racing to develop vaccines and treatments against the Bundibugyo strain, with Oxford University saying on Friday that the first volunteer group had received an experimental vaccine targeting the strain.

Several other candidate vaccines are being fast-tracked for clinical trials, while two potential treatments are also under development.

A circus performer was airlifted to a hospital after his colleague missed her target and hit him in the neck with an arrow while performing in New York, according to authorities.

The incident happened as Edwin Cuervo Rangel, 38, and Ana Daza Tavera, 42, were performing at the Orange County Fair in the town of Wallkill at around 9:30 p.m. on Friday, New York State Police said in a press release.

Cuervo Rangel and Daza Tavera are married, according to News 12.

The two performers from Wisconsin were doing a stunt when Daza Tavera shot an arrow at a foam target that Cuervo Rangel was holding, according to police.

TOURIST DIES AT LUXURY RESORT AFTER COBRA FROM SNAKE SHOW CLIMBS UP PANTS, BITES HIM: POLICE

A circus performer was airlifted to a hospital after his wife and colleague missed her target and hit him in the neck with an arrow. (Orange County Fair/Facebook)

The arrow struck and injured Cuervo Rangel, police said.

Cuervo Rangel was airlifted to Westchester Medical Center in stable condition.

A ringmaster for the traveling show company, Circus Murcia, later said the arrow hit Cuervo Rangel in his neck.

"Well, last night, unfortunately, when she shot the crossbow, it caught him in his neck," Circus Murcia Ringmaster Benjamin Jackson told News 12.

LOUISIANA WOMAN HOSPITALIZED AFTER ROPE SWING MISHAP ON CRUISE EXCURSION LEFT HER WITH GENITAL TRAUMA

Edwin Cuervo Rangel was airlifted to a hospital in stable condition. (Orange County Fair/Facebook)

"The good news is, she caught him right at the very corner of the neck. There was no blood, nothing," he added.

Circus Murcia owner Alexander Murcia said Cuervo Rangel is expected to make a full recovery.

"Our thoughts remain with him during his recovery, and we sincerely appreciate the outstanding care provided by the first responders, medical team, and everyone who assisted," Murcia told the Hudson Valley Post.

Fox News Digital reached out to Circus Murcia for comment.

Edwin Cuervo Rangel is expected to make a full recovery. (Orange County Fair/Facebook)

Police said the incident remains under investigation.

The Orange County Fair opened on Thursday and is scheduled to be open daily through Aug. 2.

The Big Top Circus featuring Circus Murcia is new to the fair this year, featuring "breathtaking acrobatics, daring aerial performances, and world-class circus artistry," according to the fair's website.

title: Nevada man dies at famed Sequoia National Park trail after sudden emergency
excerpt:

An elderly man reportedly died Thursday after suffering a medical emergency on a popular hiking trail in California's Sequ...
body_text:
A bull bison attacks camper at Yellowstone National Park. (Credit NewsFlare)

An elderly man reportedly died Thursday after suffering a medical emergency on a popular hiking trail in California's Sequoia National Park.

The victim was identified as 79-year-old John Francis Oliver of Henderson, Nevada, a suburb of Las Vegas, the Tulare County Sheriff's Office said, according to Your Central Valley.

Oliver was found along the General Sherman Tree Trail, a one-mile path that leads to the world's largest living tree, the General Sherman Tree, according to the outlet, citing the National Park Service (NPS).

First responders rendered emergency medical aid to Oliver at the scene, but the man was eventually pronounced dead in the park, according to SFGATE.

CAUSE OF DEATH REVEALED FOR BIG SUR HIKER WHOSE BODY WAS FOUND NAKED ON REMOTE CALIFORNIA TRAIL

The General Sherman giant sequoia tree stands in the Giant Forest in Sequoia National Park near Three Rivers, Calif., on October 22, 2021. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

The Tulare County Sheriff's Office declined to release additional details about what led to the medical emergency or the circumstances surrounding Oliver's death "out of respect for the family," SFGATE reported.

The man’s cause of death has also not yet been determined.

PARK VISITORS FACE FLOOD DANGER OUT WEST WHILE SEVERE STORMS RIP THROUGH NY, NJ

Sequoia National Park, home to Giant Forest and Mount Whitney, hosts the largest tree in the world.  (iStock)

The incident came as temperatures in the region climbed into the upper 90s, according to the National Weather Service.

An extreme heat warning was also in effect Thursday for portions of the nearby Mojave Desert and Indian Wells Valley.

Thursday's death marks the latest in a string of fatal incidents at Sequoia National Park and nearby areas in recent months.

LONE SURVIVOR RESCUED AFTER FATAL FALL KILLS THREE CLIMBERS ON MOUNT MCKINLEY

Visitors walk in Crescent Meadow in Sequoia National Park, California, on Monday, June 30, 2025. (Paul Bersebach/MediaNews Group/Orange County Register via Getty Images)

In June, a 17-year-old girl died after slipping into a fast-moving river during her first visit to Sequoia National Park, according to a GoFundMe.

In neighboring Kings Canyon National Park, a San Mateo couple drowned at Roaring River Falls in May, according to Fox 2 San Francisco.

Last summer, NPS also said a local missing hiker, 36, was found dead in Sequoia National Park.

Fox News Digital contacted the National Park Services and the Sequoia National Park for more information.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Argentinian leader calls Brazilian president a 'thief' and a 'convict'
excerpt:
Javier Milei (left) was in Brazil for the launch of Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign

Brazil has recalled its ambassador to Buenos Aires after Argentina's president hit out at the Brazilian pr...
body_text:
Javier Milei (left) was in Brazil for the launch of Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign

Brazil has recalled its ambassador to Buenos Aires after Argentina's president hit out at the Brazilian president, referring to him as a "thief" and a "convict".

Javier Milei made the comments on Sunday at a rally in Sao Paulo to launch the presidential campaign of right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro,  who is set to run in an election in October.

Without naming Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva explicitly, he referred to the Brazilian president derogatorily while speaking alongside Bolsonaro, who he went on to say was the only one who could "stop Lula".

Brazilian diplomats later said the Argentine leader had insulted Brazil's government, its people, and its democracy.

Speaking later on Sunday, Lula said he would continue to lead "without anyone's interference," and that "in Brazil, we do not accept anyone sticking their nose where it doesn't belong".

Brazil's ambassador to Argentina, Julio Bitelli, was due to return home between Sunday and Monday, AFP reported.

Flavio Bolsanaro is the son of Brazil's former president, Jair Bolsonaro, who was last year sentenced to more than 27 years in jail for plotting a coup aimed at keeping him in power after he lost the last election to Lula.

The judge who oversaw the conviction of Jair Bolsonaro, Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, was also referred to by Milei as "bald trash".

Moraes had also previously denied Milei permission to visit the former president while he was under house arrest in Brasilia.

In 2018, Lula was sentenced to 12 years in prison over a massive corruption and bribery scandal, but was released after serving a little over 18 months.

Lula's convictions were annulled by the Supreme Court in 2021 and in presidential elections the following year he narrowly beat far-right incumbent Jair Bolsonaro, winning 50.9% of the vote.

title: Search intensifies for North Carolina physical therapist who vanished during Caribbean getaway
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A North Carolina woman has vanished while on a trip to the Caribbean island of Grenada, sparking an urgent search as h...
body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A North Carolina woman has vanished while on a trip to the Caribbean island of Grenada, sparking an urgent search as her family, friends and loved ones plead for her safe return.

Elizabeth "Liz" Waddell, 44, was last seen Wednesday at Grand Anse Beach in St. George's, near where she was staying in the Grand Anse area, according to the Royal Grenada Police Force.

Waddell, a physical therapist, wife and mother from the Raleigh area, is described as 5 feet 5 inches tall with short blonde hair. Authorities also released a photo showing Waddell with pink hair as they asked the public for help locating her.

According to her professional website, Waddell is the founder of Art of Movement Physical Therapy and earned a doctorate in physical therapy from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR AUSTRALIAN WOMAN WHO VANISHED AFTER SENDING MESSAGE ABOUT GOING FOR A HIKE NEAR LAS VEGAS

Liz Waddell smiles during a meal in an undated photo. (Cailen Waddell)

According to a friend who said she has known Waddell and her husband for more than 20 years, Waddell traveled to Grenada for a vacation with another friend, WRAL News reported.

Waddell's friend reportedly lost sight of her after remaining at their Airbnb to take an online course while Waddell went outside, apparently for a swim.

"She had her swimsuit on, and she went outside their Airbnb," Amanda Romano-Harmon said, according to the local outlet. "They had a pool that overlooked the bay. Liz was set up out there just sightseeing from the pool, and her friend was taking her online course. When she got through with her course, she looked up and she didn't see Liz outside, so she went outside to walk around and see where she went, and she saw her towel down on the pier. So the only thing we can think is maybe she went for a swim."

The friend reportedly became increasingly concerned over the next several hours, knowing Waddell did not have her phone with her, and eventually filed a missing-persons report.

THREE SISTERS FOUND DEAD IN OCEAN AT POPULAR TOURIST BEACH AS POLICE PROBE MYSTERIOUS TRAGEDY

Liz Waddell and her husband, Cailen, pose together for a photo during a trip.  (Cailen Waddell)

Waddell's husband, Cailen, was at work when he received the call about his wife's disappearance, according to the report.

He said on social media Friday that he was heading to the area to assist in the search and urged anyone with connections to the island to share information that could help locate her.

He also described Waddell as a kind-hearted person while speaking with local Grenada media outlets.

"My wife is a loving, free-spirited person. She could make friends with anyone. She often did," he told Grenada Broadcasting Network (GBN).

Police are urging anyone with information about Waddell's whereabouts to come forward, specifically asking fishermen, boat operators and residents along Grenada's southern coastline to report any sightings that could assist in the search.

KENTUCKY MAN CHARGED WITH BOATING UNDER THE INFLUENCE AFTER FEMALE PASSENGER, 19, GOES MISSING

Grenada officials issued a missing persons alert for Liz Waddell on July 23, 2026. (Royal Grenada Police Force)

According to GBN, an extensive search effort is underway with the assistance of police officers, divers and students from St. George's University.

The U.S. State Department told Fox News Digital on Sunday that officials are aware of reports of a missing American citizen in Grenada and emphasized that the Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of U.S. citizens abroad.

The State Department declined to provide additional details due to privacy considerations but said it can assist families and friends with filing missing persons reports and help them understand local procedures.

Aradia Fitness, where Waddell also works as a fitness instructor,  called the news of her disappearance "disheartening" in a social media post and said the community is praying for her safe return.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the South Saint George Police Station at 444-4454, the Criminal Investigation Department at 440-3921, the police emergency line at 911, or the nearest police station, the Royal Grenada Police Force said.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: NBA star rips socialist NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani as 'mayor playing president' after Netanyahu video
excerpt:
Dan Dakich reacts to Nancy Armour bringing up Emmett Till in an article about Caitlin Clark & her effect on the WNBA

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's remarks about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin...
body_text:
Dan Dakich reacts to Nancy Armour bringing up Emmett Till in an article about Caitlin Clark & her effect on the WNBA

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's remarks about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu drew criticism over the weekend from an unlikely source: Milwaukee Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma, who mocked the democratic socialist as a "mayor playing president."

Responding to the mayor's video on X, the nine-year NBA veteran suggested Mamdani was more concerned with appearances than governing, labeling the mayor's talking points as performative.

Kyle Kuzma No. 18 of the Milwaukee Bucks looks to drive against the Atlanta Hawks during the first quarter at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Ga., on Jan. 19, 2026. (Getty Images)

Kyle Kuzma No. 18 of the Milwaukee Bucks walks backcourt during a game against the Dallas Mavericks at Fiserv Forum on March 5, 2025, in Milwaukee, Wis. (Getty Images)

"This is 2026. People cosplaying as things they don’t have the authority, the talent, or the track record to actually be. Just for content," Kuzma wrote, quote-tweeting Mamdani's address.

The response came after Mamdani released a video calling for the arrest of Netanyahu under an International Criminal Court warrant ahead of the United Nations General Assembly.

"A mayor playing president. A founder playing operator. A content creator playing one-on-one, thinking he’s a pro. A 25-year-old with a ring light playing economist. Everyone auditioning. Nobody building. We're raising a generation that is learning the reward isn’t in doing the thing; it’s in looking like you did the thing.

MAMDANI SAYS NYC IS EXPLORING WHETHER IT CAN ARREST NETANYAHU IF ISRAELI LEADER VISITS FOR UN GENERAL ASSEMBLY

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a still image taken from handout video released on July 21, 2026. (Reuters)

"The clip is the career. The pose is the product. The soundbite is the substitute for a life's work. Don't fall for distractions."

The comments were in line with Kuzma's growing reputation as one of the NBA's few active players willing to publicly challenge progressive political ideas, a lane many of the league's most prominent stars have largely avoided.

The same video also generated support from elsewhere in the NBA.

Days earlier, Dallas Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving and San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama were seen liking Mamdani's Instagram post, in which he called Netanyahu "the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people" and urged authorities to arrest him if he enters New York City.

KNICKS STAR KARL ANTHONY-TOWNS REPORTEDLY ATTENDS JEWISH FUNDRAISER AS OTHER NBA PLAYERS TAKE OPPOSITE STAND

OutKick contacted representatives for both players for comment but did not receive a response.

Mamdani has faced sustained criticism from Jewish organizations and political opponents over his rhetoric on Israel, accusing them of genocide.

KYRIE IRVING, VICTOR WEMBANYAMA LIKE MAMDANI'S VIDEO CALLING NETANYAHU A 'WAR CRIMINAL'

Israel rejects the ICC's jurisdiction, while Netanyahu has repeatedly denied the court's allegations.

Although Mamdani previously directed the city's legal department to examine whether New York police could enforce the warrant, he later acknowledged that the city has no legal authority to arrest visiting foreign leaders.

Kyle Kuzma of the Milwaukee Bucks reacts after being called for a foul against the Washington Wizards during the second half at Capital One Arena on Jan. 29, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Getty Images)

Critics have argued Mamdani should instead focus on issues inside New York City, including crime, sanitation and housing affordability, rather than weighing in on international conflicts beyond the mayor's authority.

Kuzma's "mayor playing president" dig offered a strong contrast to the support Mamdani's message received from Irving and Wembanyama, illustrating how the mayor's rhetoric has divided prominent voices around the NBA.

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

title: Man faces murder charge after innocent 12-year-old is killed in Bronx street gunfire
excerpt:
Video shows William Ferrer being escorted by detectives after his arrest in the fatal Bronx shooting that killed 12-year-old Jacob Freytes and wounded two other men. Credit: WNYW

A man has been charg...
body_text:
Video shows William Ferrer being escorted by detectives after his arrest in the fatal Bronx shooting that killed 12-year-old Jacob Freytes and wounded two other men. Credit: WNYW

A man has been charged with murder after a 12-year-old boy was killed by a stray bullet while riding his bicycle in the Bronx, as newly released surveillance video captures the desperate moments after he was struck.

William Ferrer, 45, was arrested Sunday morning and charged with murder, two counts of attempted murder, manslaughter, six counts of assault and three counts of criminal possession of a weapon, the New York Police Department confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Police say Ferrer is accused of opening fire during a chaotic confrontation outside Wanda Deli Grocery on Elliot Place near the Grand Concourse in the Mount Eden neighborhood Saturday afternoon, killing 12-year-old Jacob Freytes, who investigators say was an innocent bystander.

According to police, Freytes had been riding his bicycle near the bodega when gunfire erupted shortly before 5 p.m. He was struck in the shoulder and rushed to NYC Health and Hospitals/Lincoln, where he was pronounced dead.

THREE CHILDREN SHOT NEAR PUBLIC POOL IN SMALL ARKANSAS TOWN, SUSPECT TAKEN INTO CUSTODY

William Ferrer faces murder and multiple other charges after police say he fatally shot 12-year-old Jacob Freytes during a Bronx street shooting. (WNYW)

NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch announced Ferrer's arrest Sunday, calling Freytes' death "an act of senseless gun violence."

SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

"Jacob was an innocent bystander on his bike when he was taken from his family yesterday in an act of senseless gun violence," Tisch wrote on X. "No arrest can ever ease the pain of this unimaginable loss, but the NYPD will continue to do everything in our power to seek justice for Jacob."

Surveillance video shared by United Bodegas of America shows Jacob exiting the neighborhood bodega after buying a ball and getting on his bicycle.

WITNESSES RECOUNT 'SCARY' NYC STABBING AFTER SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY YELLED 'ALLAHU AKBAR' DURING ATTACKS

Police arrested William Ferrer on murder and other charges in the fatal shooting of 12-year-old Jacob Freytes, who investigators say was an innocent bystander struck by a stray bullet. (WNYW)

Moments later, as gunfire erupts, the video appears to show Freytes running back inside clutching his chest before collapsing to the floor as horrified customers look on.

The gunfire also wounded two other men. Police said a 34-year-old was shot in the foot, while a 25-year-old was struck in the buttocks. Both men were in stable condition.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani mourned Freytes' death in a statement posted to X following the shooting.

"My heart breaks for his family, friends and all those who loved him. Their loss is unimaginable," Mamdani wrote. "Our children should be able to ride their bikes on a nice summer day in their neighborhood without fear of being shot. We cannot accept this violence as normal."

The mayor also said he was praying for the recovery of the two surviving victims and thanked hospital staff and the NYPD "for their work to find those responsible for this heinous act."

New York City Public Advocate Jumaane Williams' office also mourned Freytes' death, saying "nothing could be more tragic."

"We mourn with 12-year-old Jacob Freytes' family," the Office of the Public Advocate wrote on social media. "Nothing could be more tragic: An innocent child on his bike, killed by a stray bullet."

The office added that "our children's safety is our collective responsibility" and called for "urgently implementing the strategies proven to make us safer."

Ferrer has had multiple prior run-ins with law enforcement dating back to 1999, according to the New York Post, which cited law enforcement sources. The outlet reported his record includes arrests on allegations of drug possession, drunken driving, possession of stolen property, menacing and criminal contempt.

Community members gathered outside the Bronx bodega where 12-year-old Jacob Freytes was fatally shot while riding his bicycle. (WNYW)

Fernando Mateo, spokesman for the United Bodegas of America, called Freytes' death a devastating reminder of the toll gun violence continues to take on New York City during a Sunday press conference outside the bodega where the shooting happened.

"We're just tired of having these press conferences speaking about gun violence," Mateo said. "Whether it's in a bodega, whether it is in a cab, it's gun violence on our streets."

Mateo said surveillance video shows Freytes entering the neighborhood bodega to buy a ball before walking outside moments before the shooting erupted.

"He runs back into the bodega because he lives in the area, and he's a regular in that bodega seeking refuge," Mateo said. "But no, he didn't make it. Twelve years old."

Mateo also said the store is equipped with one of the emergency panic buttons installed in many New York City bodegas, but the violence unfolded within seconds.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Athletics' Shea Langeliers, top MLB trade deadline target, could be out for season after devastating injury
excerpt:

One of MLB’s top ...
body_text:
New York Yankees infielder Jose Caballero got into a heated discussion with a home plate umpire about his pitch clock antics on Wednesday. (This video contains AI-assisted content.)

One of MLB’s top trade candidates ahead of the Aug. 3 deadline might be out for the remainder of the season.

Athletics catcher Shea Langeliers, who was enjoying a career year behind the dish and in the batter’s box, suffered a torn meniscus that could force him to miss the rest of the season, per ESPN.

The 28-year-old hurt his knee while running on the basepaths, and now he and the team are deliberating over whether he should undergo surgery to repair the tear in the knee.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Shea Langeliers of the Athletics is seen in the dugout after hitting a solo home run in the eighth inning during a game against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, in Phoenix, Ariz. (MLB Photos)

If surgery is the decision, ESPN reports it would be the end of Langeliers’ 2026 campaign.

But either way, teams that were interested in potentially trading for the All-Star catcher are very likely out of the running now. Langeliers is considered one of the best at his position in MLB, which is why the A’s had no plan to move him despite a 44-60 record on the year that puts them on the outside looking in at playoffs.

REDS' DANE MYERS CARTED OFF FIELD AFTER CRASHING INTO WALL MAKING ACROBATIC CATCH VS BREWERS

Langeliers has been the team’s top player, representing them at his first-ever All-Star Game earlier this month. And he’s doing so while others like Nick Kurtz, Brent Rooker and Jacob Wilson are dealing with injuries themselves.

Langeliers is slashing .263/.332/.497 this season with a .829 OPS, 23 home runs and 51 RBI. These are the numbers the A’s were hoping Langeliers would post this season after a successful 2025 campaign that included 31 homers and a career-high .861 OPS.

Shea Langeliers of the Athletics bats during the third inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on July 21, 2026, in Phoenix, Ariz. The Diamondbacks defeated the Athletics 6-5. (Getty Images)

He was on pace to break some more career highs, but this injury puts a damper in it all.

And those postseason contenders are just as bummed if they were hoping the A’s would change their position about moving Langeliers before the deadline. The New York Yankees, for one, are a team that’s expected to be in the catching market before the deadline, and calling the A’s about Langeliers would likely have occurred.

Now, catchers like Colorado Rockies’ Hunter Goodman and Baltimore Orioles’ Adley Rutschman could see an uptick in interest among teams hoping to bolster that position for a playoff push.

Shea Langeliers #23 of the Athletics gets ready in the batter's box against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix, Ariz., on July 20, 2026. (Getty Images)

The A’s will have to go with Jonah Heim moving forward with Langeliers sidelined, and he himself has been among trade conversations as well due to his veteran prowess. He vaults to a starting role, though, and may not be as available.

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

Nickelodeon actress Jennifer Hyatt Tedmori pulled back the curtain on life after child star status.

Tedmori, 37, warned social media followers earlier this week about a "crashout incoming" as she sifted through residual checks from her time on the popular kids' sitcom, "Ned's Declassified School Survival Guide."

"POV: You were on a TV show 20 years ago and a random envelope still shows up in your mailbox," she captioned a video before revealing the paltry sum.

'MARRIED... WITH CHILDREN' STAR TED MCGINLEY REVEALS HE GETS PENNY RESIDUAL CHECKS FROM HIS HIT TV SHOWS

Jennifer Hyatt Tedmori revealed her shocking residual income from starring on a popular Nickelodeon sitcom. (Jeffrey Mayer)

"Time to open my latest Ned’s Declassified residual checks," Tedmori wrote. "Residual checks are one of those weird parts of being a child actor that people are always curious about, so I figured I’d open them with you."

She added, "Who’s ready to find out if I’m buying coffee... or a yacht?"

Holding a thick stack of unopened mail, Tedmori explained her woes with the television world.

LISA KUDROW STILL EARNS $20M A YEAR IN RESIDUALS FROM 'FRIENDS' MORE THAN 30 YEARS AFTER SHOW PREMIERED

"I have been procrastinating opening this for months because it is a b----h," she told her followers. "Some of these could be a penny, some of these could be $5."

After opening a piece of mail and detailing the episode she was receiving the check for, Tedmori revealed a two-cent paycheck.

A post shared by Jennifer Hyatt Tedmori (@missrockdoll)

"All of two cents," she said. "See. All this paper I'm just littering in my car ... I know, hard times. The economy is s--- ... keep it. I don't want it."

‘PARENT TRAP’ STAR HAYLEY MILLS LOST HER DISNEY FORTUNE TO ‘THE TAX MAN’

Tedmori continued opening mail where she received a .63 cent check, and another check for "video projects and school clubs" returned a three-cent check.

"So for 'Ned's Declassified,' that earned me a grand total of $8.63," she said while holding a microphone in her car. "With '90210,' $30.06. Maybe I can go buy a coffee at Starbucks."

title: Cash-strapped DNC shelled out more than $800K to non-voting territories like Virgin Islands while in debt
excerpt:
Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee chair Rep. Suzan DelBene, in a Fox News Digital interview, says her party will ‘ hold Republicans accountable’ in the 2026 midterm elections.

The Democrati...
body_text:
Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee chair Rep. Suzan DelBene, in a Fox News Digital interview, says her party will ‘ hold Republicans accountable’ in the 2026 midterm elections.

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) entered the final 100 days before the midterm elections Sunday at its Washington headquarters with debts exceeding cash by more than $2 million and no plans for its customary transfers to congressional campaign committees, after an early-spending strategy raised questions about support for House candidates in decisive swing districts.

Federal Election Commission filings showed the DNC ended June with $16.3 million in cash and $18.5 million in debts, leaving liabilities approximately $2.2 million above its reserves. The Republican National Committee (RNC), by comparison, reported approximately $128.5 million on-hand and no outstanding debt.

The New York Times reported that the DNC had asked vendors to delay spending bills until after the elections and informed congressional leaders it would not make its traditional transfers to the House and Senate campaign committees.

The New York Times also noted that the DNC and an affiliated committee spent approximately $840,000 on Democratic organizations in five non-voting U.S. territories since last year.

Incoming DCCC chair Rep. Suzan DelBene, D-Wash., flanked by Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Rep. Katherine Clark, D-Mass., speaks during a news conference at the DCCC on Wednesday, December 21, 2022. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

NRCC REPORTING RECORD $47.1 MILLION QUARTER, RECORD $28.1 MILLION RAISED IN MARCH

Veteran DNC member Donna Brazile told The New York Times that DNC Chairman Ken Martin needed major assistance.

"Ken needs help — H-E-L-P," Brazile said. "And if he’s reluctant to say it, I’m here to help him ask. It’s hard. It’s very difficult."

The cash disparity extends to the committees directing resources into House races. The National Republican Congressional Committee ended June with $92.7 million, compared with $79 million for the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, Axios reported.

A recent Supreme Court decision allowing unlimited coordinated spending between parties and candidates made committee reserves more consequential in competitive districts. Control of the House could turn on fewer than 20 races, according to The Associated Press.

Despite the cash gap, Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) Chair Suzan DelBene pointed to the committee's second-quarter fundraising and the performance of Democratic candidates.

Democratic National Committee chair Ken Martin is interviewed by Fox News Digital, on July 23, 2025, at DNC headquarters in Washington D.C. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

SUPREME COURT STRIKES DOWN LIMIT ON PARTY CAMPAIGN SPENDING IN COORDINATION WITH CANDIDATES

"The DCCC's strong quarter of fundraising combined with the incredible results of our Frontliners and challengers show that across the battlefield," DelBene said, in a July press release. "Democrats are assembling people-powered campaigns ready to win in November and make Hakeem Jeffries the next speaker of the House."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, DNC Executive Director Roger Lau disputed the characterization of the vendor discussions as evidence of financial distress.

"This is nothing more than standard negotiations with vendors over contracts and payment processes," Lau said.

Democrats are trying to win back control of the House for the first time since Republicans re-gained the majority in 2022. Republicans also control the U.S. Senate after winning the majority in 2024.

Midterm elections are historically difficult for the party of the incumbent president. President Joe Biden's Democrats overperformed expectations in 2022 and held onto Senate control, but still lost the House. President Donald Trump's Republicans lost the House in 2018, his first midterm, and President Barack Obama's Democrats were routed in both his midterms as well, losing the Senate in 2014 and the House in 2010.

The 2026 midterms will determine control of the House and Senate, shaping President Donald Trump's legislative agenda during the final two years of his term. (Al Drago/Getty Images)

DEMOCRATS’ MIDTERM PUSH CLOUDED BY INFIGHTING OVER PARTY KEEPING 2024 AUTOPSY UNDER WRAPS

The DNC said its territorial spending was part of a four-year State Partnership Program that transfers more than $1 million per month to 57 Democratic state and territorial parties. Each party receives $17,500 monthly, while parties in Republican-controlled states receive an additional $5,000 through the DNC’s Red State Fund. State parties also receive six figures’ worth of voter data and technology annually.

The agreement also provides for six regional training boot camps during each two-year cycle and five new regional directors.

Martin said last week that the investment reflected his strategy of moving resources beyond Washington and strengthening local party organizations.

"The current DNC has raised the most money of any DNC without the White House in the 198-year history of the Democratic Party," Martin said in a Substack post on Monday. "If the question is whether the Democratic Party will be ready to win — everywhere, at every level, in this election and for the decade ahead — the answer is a resounding yes."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The committee's financial position received additional scrutiny Sunday when digital news publication NOTUS reported that the DNC used its headquarters as collateral for a $15 million credit line. A DNC official said the building had also secured credit lines in several previous election cycles.

"This is not new," the official said. "The loan documents were publicly released in November, and the DNC’s building was also used as collateral in our prior lines of credit in 2019, 2018, 2014, and many other years."

Fox News Digital reached out to the RNC for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

CJ Womack is an associate editor at Fox News.

CJ joined Fox News Digital's team in 2026, which highlights the vital role journalism plays in shaping politics and culture. He has years of experience analyzing and reporting on the news media.

CJ graduated from Long Beach State University in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a minor in Journalism.

You can send news tips to cj.womack@fox.com and follow CJ on Twitter.

title: AusAlert test: what time will national emergency warning siren sound on phones in Australia today? Here’s what to know
excerpt:
National emergency test alert will be sent to all compatible mobile devices on 27 July, with domestic violence advocates advising how to turn off safe phones

Follow our Australia news live blog for l...
body_text:
National emergency test alert will be sent to all compatible mobile devices on 27 July, with domestic violence advocates advising how to turn off safe phones

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Virtually every phone in the country will blare an emergency siren at 2pm AEST on Monday 27 July as part of the first Australia-wide test of a new national warning system called AusAlert.

Most phones, and some smartwatches and tablets, will receive a pop-up notification and an alert sound that cannot be silenced – even if your device is on “do not disturb” or silent mode.

The warning system will be deployed to prepare Australians for fires, floods, terrorist incidents or health emergencies – but it has raised questions about regional access and the risk it poses to women and children experiencing domestic and family violence.

AusAlert is Australia’s new national warning system, which will send emergency messages to mobile devices during local and widespread disasters.

Authorities currently use SMS texts to alert people about safety information. The new system will instead send a mass broadcast via mobile phone towers, with an alert popping up on devices, similar to a phone notification.

It will launch nationally in October, months after the national alert test.

“On Monday 27 July 2026, a test alert will be sent to all mobile devices in Australia. This includes most phones, and some smart watches and tablets,” the National Emergency Management Agency (Nema) advises.

Users will hear a siren and see a pop-up notification on their phone, which will look different depending on the device, but with text including “TEST MESSAGE” and “NO ACTION IS REQUIRED”.

“What people should expect to hear is a siren that will last for about 10 seconds,” said Pat Hetherington, the interim coordinator general at Nema.

He said it would be “loud enough to get people’s attention” but quieter than a fire alarm.

“It will be noticeable, but it won’t won’t be too over the top.”

There have been local tests, but Monday will be the first nationwide test, occurring at 2pm AEST, which is:

2pm for New South Wales, Victoria, the ACT, Queensland and Tasmania.

1.30pm in the Northern Territory and South Australia.

Hetherington said AusAlert came from a recommendation of the royal commission into the 2019-20 black summer bushfires, which called for a nationally consistent warning system.

“The existing system is based on standard SMS capability, and throughout a series of emergencies and disasters, that system has had real latency in terms of people receiving the messages,” he said.

“You [could] get network congestion, text messages may not come through in a timely way … or come through at all, dependent upon who your provider is.”

Kristy McBain, the federal emergency management minister whose electorate of Eden-Monaro was hit by the black summer bushfires, said some people in her area didn’t receive emergency text alerts during that disaster because their phone provider was unavailable.

The new system allows nationwide alerts as well as localised “geofenced” alerts such as for floods or even warnings to boil water in emergency situations.

McBain said AusAlert was a “far superior” system and would reach “more people in a more timely manner” than current warning systems used by state governments. Existing systems will still be used in future, with McBain describing AusAlert as “another tool in the toolkit”.

Essentially, yes. Hetherington said phones made after 2019 should receive the alert, but some older phones may not.

The alert will come through on all compatible devices even if you are on a call, or if the phone is on silent. Nema has advice that about 80% of Apple iPhones will ring, and some 16m Android devices.

“The only way to not receive a critical alert is to turn your mobile device off or switch it to ‘airplane mode’,” Nema advised.

iPhone models 11 and up running iOS 26.4 or later.

Apple Watch models SE2, SE3, Series 6 and up running watchOS 26.4 or later.

Android devices running Android 12 or later.

Older Androids, or those not using iOS or Android “might still receive AusAlerts”, Nema said, but Apple iPads will not.

Hetherington and Nema’s deputy coordinator general, Katarina Carroll, said the agency had engaged with “thousands” of groups including schools, businesses and even funeral associations to warn of the alert test.

They said it was important to run the test during an “ordinary” time of day so people knew what to expect in future.

But noting some people may find it inconvenient to have a loud siren ring alert, such as during an important meeting or a funeral, Hetherington and Carroll said “if you have your phone off an hour before and an hour after [2pm AEST], we’re confident you won’t receive that message”.

Other countries around the world have had problems in testing or using such systems, with alerts delayed or not arriving at all. Nema said it had “learned a lot” from tests around the world and it was well prepared for Monday.

Domestic and family violence advocates have raised concerns about the risk of the alert exposing “safe phones”, or devices kept hidden for safety reasons by those experiencing violence.

Nema said the agency had engaged with family violence experts about the test, including assisting advocates to disseminate safety information, and posting a safety guide on its website.

Hetherington said phones switched off or on airplane mode would not receive the alert, and said: “The message for safe phones and hidden phones is very much [to switch off for] a 24-hour period.”

Carroll added: “The advice is if there’s anything that’s happening [during the test], have it off for an hour or so. But certainly for domestic and family violence, there’s that broader advice for that extension of time [24 hours].”

Groups such as the Women’s Safety Commissioner, DV Connect and the Council of Single Mothers and their Children have issued safety advisories to this effect.

Nothing at all. The test requires no action.

However, Hetherington encouraged Australians to answer a survey or give feedback after the test to help Nema assess the success of the trial and any changes that may be needed.

“People should read the message. But it is a test that doesn’t require people to do anything,” he said.

“We’re obviously interested in hearing if people haven’t received the message.”

Nema suggests the warnings could be used for legitimate hazards such as bushfires, floods, cyclones and earthquakes; serious public safety issues or terrorism; biosecurity incidents; and major public health incidents.

States and territories will be able to send alerts.

“I would expect some states to use it quite a lot, particularly where you want information to get out almost in real time,” Hetherington said.

title: RAF Chinook crash victims’ families ask Andy Burnham for review of disaster
excerpt:
PM urged to end ‘cover-up culture’ and order independent review taking in evidence that has emerged on 1994 crash

The families of those killed in an RAF Chinook crash in 1994 have urged Andy Burnham ...
body_text:
PM urged to end ‘cover-up culture’ and order independent review taking in evidence that has emerged on 1994 crash

The families of those killed in an RAF Chinook crash in 1994 have urged Andy Burnham to end Britain’s “cover-up culture” and order an independent review into the disaster.

Twenty-nine serving military personnel died when the Chinook HC2 helicopter crashed on the Mull of Kintyre in south-west Scotland during a flight from Northern Ireland.

The two pilots were initially blamed for the crash but exonerated after an inquiry in 2011, which did not determine its cause.

Liam Fox, the former Conservative defence secretary who ordered that official review, said last month there were now “deep concerns” that “vital information” could have been withheld.

Fox, who is backing the calls for a fresh independent review, said there was now a “strong enough belief” that a deliberate cover-up had taken place. There were concerns, he said, that details provided by the Ministry of Defence (MoD) on the airworthiness of the Chinook that crashed were “not correct”.

A high court judge ruled this month that the families of several victims of the crash could not bring a legal claim against the MoD over the incident because it had been brought too late.

The Chinook Justice Campaign (CJC), which is made up of more than 55 family members of 25 of the victims, said it would take the case to the European court of human rights.

However, Matt Tobias, whose father, Lt Col John Tobias, was killed in the crash, said the families “do not want years of further litigation” and urged the prime minister to help by ordering a fresh independent review.

He said: “We would urge Mr Burnham to meet us within his first 100 days in office so we can present the evidence that has emerged over recent years and explain why we believe a fresh review, independent of the Ministry of Defence, is now essential.

“Mr Burnham’s speech in the House of Commons, in which he spoke about ending Britain’s cover-up culture and strengthening the duty of candour, gave our families real hope.”

In a letter delivered to Burnham, the Chinook families said it could be a “test case” for the new Hillsborough law, which was unanimously backed by MPs this month and creates a legally enforceable duty of candour compelling public officials and authorities to act transparently during investigations.

Tobias said: “We ask that he and his ministers give the Chinook families more respect than we received from his predecessor, who denied us a meeting and an inquiry – believing MoD lies instead. After 32 years, we are not asking for special treatment. We are simply asking for the truth.”

The CJC group said it wanted Burnham to establish a fresh review, independent of the Ministry of Defence, with full access to all relevant documents relating to the airworthiness of the Chinook helicopter and the circumstances leading up to the crash.

An MoD spokesperson said: “Our thoughts and sympathies remain with the families, friends, and colleagues of all those who died in the Mull of Kintyre crash.

“We understand the recent court judgment will be disappointing for those involved. Defence Ministers have previously met with the CJC and we will continue to engage to hear concerns and discuss this important matter.”

title: Rising oil prices could force up UK interest rates, say economists
excerpt:
Bank of England expected to keep rates on hold on Thursday but renewed Iran conflict casts shadow over energy costs

The Bank of England could be forced to tear up its economic forecasts and raise int...
body_text:
Bank of England expected to keep rates on hold on Thursday but renewed Iran conflict casts shadow over energy costs

The Bank of England could be forced to tear up its economic forecasts and raise interest rates later this year if oil prices return to above $100 a barrel, according to City economists.

Before a meeting of Bank officials on Thursday, economists said that while an interest rate hike would probably be avoided this week there could be some in the future because of conflict in the Middle East.

The UK economy has remained relatively resilient since Donald Trump’s war on Iran began in March, but this could be at risk after fighting reignited last week, the economists added.

The breakdown of the fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran sent oil prices back to the highs seen in April and May, sparking fears that higher prices at the pumps would send inflation soaring.

A barrel of Brent crude jumped above $100 a barrel (£75) on Thursday before falling back to $96 on Friday, well above the $71 recorded earlier this month.

Gas prices have soared before the crucial period when most European countries refill their storage facilities in time for winter heating demand.

All the major central banks say they are concerned about the impact of the war in the Middle East and its influence on rising prices.

The Bank’s nine-member monetary policy committee is expected to vote on Thursday in favour of holding interest rates, and to continue maintaining them at 3.75% until at least December, by a margin of seven to two. This echoes their last meeting in June when two officials on the committee voted to increase rates to head off rising inflation.

Sanjay Raja, the chief UK economist at Deutsche Bank, said that calculation might change if the intensity of airstrikes was maintained and the sea channels allowing tankers to enter and exit oil terminals remained blocked.

He said: “We see upside risks to the interest rate outlook in the near term, with much dependent on the duration of the unfolding energy shock. A second energy wave will likely amplify uncertainty around the inflation path and the risk of second-round effects.”

George Buckley, the chief UK and euro area economist at Nomura, said financial markets were giving a clear signal that higher oil prices would translate into higher interest rates. “At $90 they would see the need for one and a half quarter-point hikes. At $100 there would be a need for two 25 basis point hikes,” he said.

Mohamed El-Erian, a professor at the University of Pennsylvania and a former chief economist at the International Monetary Fund, suggested a sustained increase in oil prices to $90 a barrel could be enough to rewrite UK policymakers’ forecasts.

He said: “Should oil prices remain above $90 a barrel, an important ‘if’, then headline inflation would face significant upward pressure. This, in turn, would heighten concerns over immediate indirect effects, including rising food prices driven by diesel transportation costs, and broader second-round effects over time.

“The result would be heightened market expectation of a Bank of England rate hike, even as higher energy prices act as a tax on economic activity.”

Ruth Gregory, the deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said a worst-case scenario showed that if inflation rose to 7% over the coming months in response to the Middle East conflict, UK interest rates would probably rise from 3.75% to 4.75%.

Harvinder Kalirai, the chief global currency strategist at Alpine Macro, a division of Oxford Economics, said he expected the Bank to “look through the oil shock and political noise” to hold rates steady for now before resuming cuts next year.

He said the UK was not strong enough to withstand a rise in the cost of fuel and higher interest rates: “Demand is not strong enough to sustain a pass-through from the energy shock, forcing firms to absorb higher input costs.”

Kalirai said once volatile elements of the inflation basket – including fuel and food – were excluded, prices were growing slowly while pay packets were rising at a slower pace.

Costas Milas, an economics professor at the University of Liverpool, said oil price shocks triggered long bouts of inflation and should be tackled quickly.

He said: “This is too uncomfortable for the BoE to stay inactive not least because the public remains dissatisfied with the BoE. Since dissatisfaction increases with inflation, the BoE should act soon by raising interest rates, possibly as early as September.”

David Aikman, the head of the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “The longer inflation remains above target, the greater the change inflation expectations shift and wages respond – and hence the Bank needing to hike rates.”

Financial markets also anticipate a hike at the European Central Bank governing council’s next meeting on 10 September. It raised interest rates in June for the first time since 2023 in response to higher inflation caused by the war in Iran.

Central banks have come under fire for considering a rise in the cost of borrowing, with critics arguing increases in interest rates will only make a bad situation worse.

title: Pentagon reports more than 600 Iran war casualties in quiet database update
excerpt:
Figures are source of dispute as US defense department days ago reduced record of troops killed and wounded

The Pentagon updated its official war casualty database over the weekend, adding more than ...
body_text:
Figures are source of dispute as US defense department days ago reduced record of troops killed and wounded

The Pentagon updated its official war casualty database over the weekend, adding more than 140 wounded service members. The Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) also introduced a new casualty category labeled “Overseas Operations” for personnel killed and wounded “starting July 7”.

According to the updated database, the official toll for the earlier phase of the US-Iran war, known as Operation Epic Fury, now stands at 14 service members killed and more than 400 wounded in action.

These figures have been the point of contention after the Pentagon previously reduced the totals from 18 deaths and 482 wounded that had been recorded just days earlier.

The dispute comes after the collapse of the ceasefire with Iran and the resumption of near-daily airstrikes beginning on 6 July. Analysts and officials have questioned whether casualties from the renewed fighting should be counted separately from Operation Epic Fury, a move that would be unprecedented.

The Trump administration is seeking to classify the renewed military campaign as separate from Operation Epic Fury, the US military’s official name for the Iran conflict.

The change is tied to the War Powers Act of 1973, which requires the president to end military operations within 60 days unless Congress authorizes an extension. The Trump administration has argued that the April ceasefire with Iran paused the clock on 1 May for the conflict’s initial period. The separate casualty count beginning on 7 July follows that interpretation.

The shift became apparent earlier this week when the Pentagon’s official online list of service members killed in the ongoing Iran war did not include the four soldiers who died during renewed fighting over the weekend. Their names, however, were included in a Pentagon press release announcing the formal transfer of their remains back to the US on Wednesday.

Combined with the updated Operation Epic Fury totals, the new Pentagon figures show that 18 US troops have been killed and 624 wounded since the US launched its war against Iran on 28 February.

Lawmakers from both parties have challenged the administration’s interpretation of the War Powers Act timeline.

Thomas Massie, a Republican House member from Kentucky, responded to the updated numbers in an X post, writing: “Let me explain this absurd ruse: The Pentagon is pretending there have been two Iran wars separated by a brief cease-fire.

“The reality: By going more than 90 days without congressional authorization,” the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, “IS BREAKING THE LAW and must be held accountable”.

title: Jacinta Allan expected to face leadership challenge after Victorian Labor factions meet
excerpt:
Minister says premier ‘not going anywhere’ and describes leaking of Sunday-night meeting as attempt to build momentum for spill

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breakin...
body_text:
Minister says premier ‘not going anywhere’ and describes leaking of Sunday-night meeting as attempt to build momentum for spill

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Labor premier, Jacinta Allan, is expected to face a leadership challenge when state parliament resumes this week, though supporters insist she is “not going anywhere”.

Just four months out from a state election, factional conveners from Labor’s left and right met on Sunday night to discuss whether Allan still had the support of a majority of the caucus. It is understood the group agreed she did not.

But the pathway to a challenge remains unclear, as Allan’s most likely opponent – the deputy premier, Ben Carroll – has indicated to colleagues he would only run for the leadership if the position were vacant.

One option being floated by the factions on Sunday was for a group of ministers to approach Allan on Monday before a planned cabinet meeting to inform her she had lost the support of her colleagues.

It was their hope that she would stand down before a vote during Tuesday’s caucus meeting, the first day of parliament after the winter break.

But if Allan contested a leadership ballot, the entire Victorian Labor membership would also get a vote in a weeks-long process, thanks to rule changes introduced after the instability of the Rudd-Gillard-Rudd era. The rules have been untested.

One minister close to Allan maintained she was “not going anywhere” and described the leaking of the meeting as an attempt to build momentum for a spill. Another said not all parliamentarians within the left faction were consulted before the meeting and that there was “no uniform position” within the grouping.

“There is no vacancy, no challenger and no consolidated position within the left,” the minister said. “It’s just one big smoke machine.”

The attorney general, Sonya Kilkenny, a key supporter of the premier, said leadership speculation was “idle gossip” earlier on Sunday.

“She has my full support, and this idle gossip doesn’t help Victorians,” Kilkenny said. “It is only hurting Victorians at a time when Victorians need us all to be focused on them, and that is exactly what Jacinta Allan and our Labor government, our team, is doing.”

Allan became premier after the resignation of Daniel Andrews in September 2023.

Momentum had been building for a leadership spill before parliament rose for a winter break in June due to poor polling and Allan’s weak personal approval ratings, rising support for One Nation and concerns about her response to organised crime infiltrating the state’s Big Build, via the construction union.

Allan, who previously served as the minister for transport infrastructure overseeing the Big Build, has rejected growing calls for a royal commission.

But Carroll ruled out a challenge at the time, at an awkward press conference where he looked Allan in the eye and declared he would not challenge her for the leadership.

At the same 15 June press conference, he told reporters: “I’ve got a young daughter at home, and I couldn’t be more proud to make sure she grows up knowing that I supported Jacinta Allan to be a world-class premier and get re-elected in her own right.”

It is understood Carroll, if elected leader, would immediately call for a royal commission, work to resolve the pay dispute between the state government and public school teachers, and attempt to improve the party’s economic credentials and standing with the business community.

title: Boy, 16, charged with murder of teenager stabbed in Luton park
excerpt:
Four others arrested on suspicion of same murder in Luton after death of 17-year-old

A 16-year-old boy has been charged with murdering a teenager who died from multiple stab wounds at a park in Luton...
body_text:
Four others arrested on suspicion of same murder in Luton after death of 17-year-old

A 16-year-old boy has been charged with murdering a teenager who died from multiple stab wounds at a park in Luton, police said.

Four other teenagers have been arrested on suspicion of the same murder.

Bedfordshire police said officers were called to Kingsway recreation ground shortly after 6.30pm on Friday following reports that a number of teenagers were seen “carrying large knives”.

The 17-year-old boy, who has yet to be identified, was taken to hospital but died a short time later.

Police said two boys, aged 16 and 17, had been arrested on suspicion of murder on Saturday after they were initially arrested on suspicion of violent disorder.

The younger male has since been charged with murder and remanded in custody, the force said.

Another three 17-year-old boys have also been arrested, each on suspicion of murder, violent disorder and carrying a weapon, it added in its statement on Sunday.

DCI Nick Gardener said: “We are progressing our investigation and we are continuing to appeal to anyone who was in the area, or witnessed the events leading up to the disorder, to please get in touch.

“Our officers are continuing to carry out additional high-visibility patrols, and we are continuing to engage with local members of the public.

“We would also like to remind the public not to share any distressing videos or images as this can be concerning for families involved, but also form a vital part of the police investigation.”

Zanib Raja, a councillor in Luton, has also encouraged people not to share alleged videos of the incident online.

Raja wrote on Facebook: “Like many of you, I became aware of this horrific attack through disturbing videos circulating online.

“Let me say this clearly: Do not share them. They traumatise the family, fuel fear, & do nothing to help.”

She added: “A tragic incident took place … in Kingsway Park, a place many of us grew up in, played in, & built memories in.

“A place that should be safe for families, children, & every resident of our town. Instead, a man lost his life in broad daylight. A family has been shattered. Luton is hurting.”

title: Former NSW Liberal powerbroker at heart of Icac allegations now living in UK and not expected to appear
excerpt:
Christian Ellis, a former registered lobbyist, is named in two Independent Commission Against Corruption allegations

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news emai...
body_text:
Christian Ellis, a former registered lobbyist, is named in two Independent Commission Against Corruption allegations

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A key figure at the centre of an anti-corruption inquiry involving the New South Wales Liberal party has moved to the UK and is not expected to give evidence during eight weeks of public hearings.

The Independent Commission Against Corruption will start its Operation Rosny hearings on Monday. The first witness will be a hotelier, Michael O’Hara, followed later in the week by a former Liberal staffer, Dylan Whitelaw, and a consultant, Robert Assaf.

O’Hara and Assaf are among 10 individuals Icac has said it is investigating. Whitelaw is not named in the Icac allegations.

Christian Ellis, a former registered lobbyist and Liberal powerbroker who once received a glowing endorsement from the federal opposition leader, Angus Taylor, is named in two Icac allegations but is not expected to appear.

A 2023 parliamentary inquiry preceded Icac’s current examination of “possible offences under the Electoral Funding Act”. Since that parliamentary inquiry, Ellis has moved to the UK, Guardian Australia can reveal.

Icac is investigating several allegations, firstly that Liberal figures, including Ellis and Assaf, “solicited or accepted” donations, including from prohibited donors, in amounts which were undeclared or exceeded caps, to recruit or renew members to the party – a practice known as “branch stacking”.

The corruption watchdog is examining a second allegation that between 2020 and 2023, the fugitive property developer Jean Nassif and his company, Toplace, made prohibited donations solicited or accepted by Liberals, including Ellis, “in exchange for the pursuit of outcomes sought by Mr Nassif”.

The 2023 parliamentary inquiry was prompted by allegations made in a 2022 speech under parliamentary privilege by the Liberal MP Ray Williams that Nassif had met Ellis and other senior Liberals, who were paid significant funds to arrange for new councillors to be elected to the Hills Shire council.

Ellis did not appear at the 2023 inquiry because he could not be served with summons after multiple attempts.

The inquiry’s final report recommended that Ellis be called before any future inquiry to give evidence.

Ellis, a director and shareholder of the former registered lobbying firm Beckington, whose clients included Toplace, was elected to the NSW Liberal state executive in 2019, following which he stepped down as director in favour of his wife.

In 2022, Taylor wrote an endorsement of Ellis for a position on the NSW party’s state council, saying “our party will do well to have people like Christian elected to positions of state council”. Taylor, now the federal Liberal leader, is not accused of any wrongdoing.

Ellis declined to comment when asked about the Icac allegations and his move overseas.

title: ‘Get rid of them’: One Nation senator claims party will ‘remigrate’ illegal visa holders in resurfaced interview
excerpt:
Exclusive: Malcolm Roberts uses white supremacist concept to describe the party’s plans for deporting 200,000 people from Australia

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our bre...
body_text:
Exclusive: Malcolm Roberts uses white supremacist concept to describe the party’s plans for deporting 200,000 people from Australia

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Senator Malcolm Roberts claims One Nation wants to deport at least 200,000 people and has repeatedly referred to the far-right concept of “remigration” in podcast interviews and speeches to niche platforms.

In two recent podcasts, Roberts said One Nation wanted to deport 100,000 temporary residents as well as 100,000 international students – a total much higher than the party’s published policy. The senator said after those people were removed, he wanted to “start working on the higher numbers of people we need to get rid of”.

One Nation’s policy website states the party would seek to “deport 75,000 illegal migrants”, specifically noting “visa overstayers, illegal workers, and unlawful non-residents”. The website also pledges to “end the student visa loopholes that turn study into a backdoor to permanent residency or low-wage labour”.

But Roberts, in an interview with the 2 Worlds Collide podcast in November 2025, suggested One Nation wanted to deport or “remigrate” a far higher number.

“We would also deport immediately anybody who’s here illegally, and that’s 100,000 people now … on contravention of their resident visas. That’s 100,000 we would deport, remigrate. Call it what you want. Get rid of them straight away,” he said.

“Then we’ve got about an estimated 100,000 international students who are here illegally. They’ve either graduated and not gone home or they’ve breached their legal visa. So we would send them home.”

In another interview with podcaster Brodie Buchal, published in June, Roberts repeated those sentiments.

“We have 100,000 people here on temporary resident visas illegally. We would deport them, remigrate them, send them home,” he said.

“We’ve got 100,000 students who are here illegally, and we suspect it’s much, much more. Send them home.”

“We’d tighten the entry requirements, remigrate, deport, and then start working on the higher numbers of people we need to get rid of.”

One Nation was contacted for comment and clarification of its deportation policy.

One Nation’s hardline immigration policy has come under renewed scrutiny after Pauline Hanson’s appearance on Channel 7’s Spotlight program, where she met Rupert Lowe, leader of hard-right party Restore Britain. Lowe gave her a pamphlet titled “mass deportations” and Hanson replied they were “on the same page”.

Seven reporter Liam Bartlett asked Hanson whether she thought “this concept of mass deportation is a good one?” She replied: “I love it.”

However One Nation has consistently declined to detail how it would enact such a policy. MP Barnaby Joyce on Monday said people would be deported “as it becomes apparent that they’re not supposed to be here”, including “as people present themselves for medical issues”.

Abul Rizvi, former deputy secretary of the immigration department, said it would be “eye-wateringly expensive” for a system to deport such numbers of people from Australia, or a Trump-style mass deportation operation like the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). He said recent figures showed only about 2,000 people were apprehended, detained and deported from Australia last year, with another 6,000 voluntarily leaving.

“It would cost a fortune and unless you did it carefully, it would result in massive errors and all sorts of problems,” Rizvi said.

“There is a sensible policy in this space to be developed, but you need to do it in a careful, well-targeted way that doesn’t increase in huge errors, huge numbers of people detained and clogging up court systems.”

Roberts’ recent comments have also repeatedly referenced “remigration”. The term has featured in Trump administration immigration policies, including an “office of remigration” to oversee deportations and “voluntary return of migrants” – Trump himself tweeted about his plan to return “illegal migrants to their home countries (also known as remigration)”.

But remigration has also become a buzzword for the global far right. The Global Project Against Hate and Extremism described remigration as “a white supremacist policy concept that calls for the forced removal of immigrants, refugees, and their descendants — including legal residents and citizens — based on race, ethnicity, culture, being perceived as ‘non-white,’ or a failure to ‘assimilate’.”

One Nation was contacted for comment regarding Roberts’ understanding of the term.

In addition to mentioning “remigration” on the 2 Worlds Collide and Brodie Buchal podcasts, Roberts also advocated for it during a speech to a conference organised by conservative campaign group Firebrand. Photos from that conference, posted to social media, show Hanson was also in attendance.
